studies.title: Higher incidence of paediatric autoimmune liver disease post-COVID.
studies.journal: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
studies.authors: Warner, Suz, Mtegha, Marumbo Paul, Kostova, Mariana, Jayaprakash, Kavitha et al.
studies.abstract: A higher incidence of autoimmune conditions with greater disease severity is reported post-Coronavirus Disease (COVID). The incidence and disease severity of paediatric autoimmune liver disease (AILD) post-COVID has not been assessed. Data on children <16 years of age diagnosed with AILD between 2015 and 2024 from a United Kingdom quaternary liver specialist centre was captured. Comparison of AILD incidence and presenting clinical characteristics in pre and post-COVID pandemic time-periods were made. 199 patients were newly diagnosed with AILD within the study period (82 pre-COVID [2015-2019]; 47 autoimmune hepatitis type 1 [AIH-1], 11 AIH-2, 9 primary sclerosing cholangitis [PSC], 15 overlap/autoimmune sclerosing cholangitis [ASC], and 117 post-COVID [2020-2024]; 64 AIH-1, 10 AIH-2, 20 PSC, 23 overlap/ASC). A sharp rise in the incidence of AIH-1, PSC and overlap syndrome/ASC was observed post-COVID, being most marked in the AIH-1 cohort (p < 0.0001). Children were older at disease presentation for AIH-1, PSC and overlap/ASC compared to pre-COVID, particularly in AIH-1 (p = 0.0093). Minimal variation was observed in AIH-2 patients. Most patients presenting with AIH-1 and overlap/ASC post-COVID did not have a personal history of autoimmunity. High viral coinfection rates were observed in post-COVID AIH-1 and AIH-2 presentations. The higher incidence and older presenting age of newly diagnosed AILD patients post-COVID may have resulted from immune dysregulation in susceptible children following the sudden exposure to viral infections after long periods of social isolation, triggering the onset of autoimmunity even in individuals without an autoimmune predisposition.

studies.title: Primary cilia orchestrate the multi-organ network in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
studies.authors: Zhao, Yafang, Tian, Zijiao, Dou, Dou, Li, Ruoxuan et al.
studies.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is an increasingly prevalent cause of chronic liver disease and a major driver of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide. Although its pathogenesis involves complex interactions among metabolic, inflammatory, and neuroendocrine processes across multiple organs, current therapeutic strategies remain largely liver-centric and fail to address this systemic complexity. Primary cilia (PC) are evolutionarily conserved microtubule-based organelles that function as cellular sensory hubs, integrating extracellular signals and coordinating metabolic and inflammatory pathways. Emerging evidence from studies of ciliopathies, obesity, and neurodegeneration suggests that ciliary dysfunction may contribute to metabolic disorders affecting multiple organ systems. Here, we synthesize current evidence to propose a cilia-centered conceptual framework for MASH pathogenesis. We outline a dual-axis model in which PCs coordinate a horizontal metabolic axis linking the liver, gut, and pancreas to regulate glucose and lipid homeostasis, and a vertical neuro-metabolic axis connecting the brain, gut, and liver to integrate neural and endocrine signaling. Within these networks, cilia-associated pathways, including mammalian target of rapamycin, Hedgehog, Wnt/β-catenin, Notch, and transforming growth factor beta signaling, modulate key processes underlying steatosis, inflammation, and fibrogenesis. Dysfunction of PCs in hypothalamic neurons, pancreatic β-cells, intestinal stromal cells, and hepatic stellate cells may collectively amplify metabolic imbalance and inflammatory signaling, thereby promoting MASH progression. Understanding the systemic regulatory role of PC provides a unifying perspective on the multi-organ nature of MASH and highlights cilia-associated pathways as potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

studies.title: Persistent neutrophil maturation deficits associate with cognitive impairment in individuals with post-acute sequelae of COVID-19.
studies.authors: Papatheodorou, Ioanna, Lázničková, Petra, Feglarová, Tereza, Blažková, Gabriela et al.
studies.abstract: Post-COVID-19 condition, or post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), is characterized by persistent cognitive impairments and immune dysregulation. While neutrophils are critical in acute COVID-19, whether their long-term functional dysregulation contributes to PASC, remains unclear. Thus, we investigated the links between immune system changes, symptom severity and cognitive impairment in PASC. In this cross-sectional study, we enrolled 40 individuals with self-reported issues with COVID-19 recovery (PASC) and 37 fully recovered (REC) volunteers. Participants were post-infection at either TP1 (from 6 up to 18 months post-infection, 7 PASC, 20 REC) or at TP2 (from 19 up to 36 months post-infection, 33 PASC, 17 REC). We evaluated the Newcastle post-COVID-19 Syndrome Follow Up Screening (NC) scores for symptom severity, and neuropsychological tests for memory, attention, and executive function. Peripheral blood was analyzed using multicolor flow cytometry, ELISA, clustering, and multivariate regression. PASC participants in both the TP1 cohort and the TP2 cohort, demonstrated increased NC scores and significant changes in neutrophil numbers and subset composition. studies.title: Recommendations for the primary care management of post COVID and post acute infectious syndrome: a comparative analysis of international guidelines.
studies.authors: Brand, Marlene, Bellmann-Strobl, Judith, Franke, Christiana, Scheibenbogen, Carmen et al.
studies.abstract: The medical care of people with post COVID syndrome (PCS) and other post-acute infectious syndromes (PAIS) remains a major challenge as dedicated care structures are scarce, diagnostic evaluation is often complex, and curative therapies are largely lacking. General practitioners play an essential role in initial assessment and the coordination of care and treatment. However, standardized and evidence-based recommendations specifically tailored to primary care are scarce. This study aimed to analyze and compare diagnostic and therapeutic recommendations for primary care of PCS from international guidelines. Six guidelines and recommendations were included, originating from Germany, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States, the WHO, and a European scientific society. The analysis revealed considerable variation in scope, level of detail and practical applicability. Most guidelines recommend symptom-based or exclusionary diagnostic approaches. Non-pharmacological interventions such as rehabilitation, self-management and psychological support are commonly addressed. In contrast, pharmacological options are rarely specified due to limited evidence. While the importance of general practitioners is acknowledged across documents, specific support structures and implementation strategies vary. To date, structured care recommendations for patients with Long COVID and other PAIS in primary care remain limited.

studies.title: Feasibility of a community-based physical activity programme in individuals with Long Covid: insights from the Hertfordshire longitudinal observational programme.
studies.authors: Logue, M, Lyus, R, Edwards, B
studies.abstract: This study explores the feasibility of implementing and evaluating a community-based physical activity programme for individuals with Long Covid in Hertfordshire, UK. Long Covid presents unique challenges including fluctuating symptoms, post-exertional malaise and difficulties with re-engagement following symptom flare-ups. Developed collaboratively by the Herts Sports & Physical Activity Partnership and local NHS Covid Rehabilitation Services, the programme aimed to address these challenges through tailored physical activity opportunities informed by the lived experience of Long Covid. A longitudinal observational design was used to evaluate programme retention, symptom severity, health-related quality of life and physical activity levels among 62 participants over a 12-month period. Data were collected via validated self-report tools including the EQ-5D-5L, EQ-VAS, SBQ-LC and VAS pain scale. High initial engagement was observed, with 89% of participants completing the first follow-up survey and 52% remaining engaged through to follow-up 4. While average physical activity minutes remained stable, the proportion of inactive participants declined from 37% to 25%. Statistically significant improvements were observed in self-rated health (EQ-VAS), breathing difficulties, fatigue and brain fog. Weak but significant correlations were found between increased physical activity and reduced symptom severity in several domains, including mobility, self-care and musculoskeletal pain. No significant changes were observed in anxiety or depression, suggesting physical activity alone may not address the full spectrum of Long Covid symptoms. These findings demonstrate that community-based physical activity interventions are feasible for people with Long Covid, though sustained behavioural change and mental health support remain important challenges. This study contributes practical insights for service development while highlighting the need for more rigorous controlled designs and diverse sampling in future research.

studies.title: Afterword/Afterworld: Beyond Imperial Breathlessness, Toward Abolitionist Medicine.
studies.authors: Kapadia, Ronak K
studies.abstract: This afterword theorizes immunity as a governing grammar of contemporary medicine, empire, and social life. Reading across the special issue, it traces how biomedical notions of defense, juridical exemption, and political impunity converge in an immunitary paradigm that organizes breath, care, and survivability unevenly across pandemics, settler colonial violence, racial capitalism, carcerality, and climate collapse. The essay develops the concept of imperial breathlessness to name the atmospheric condition through which empire rations breathable life, from COVID-19 triage and Long COVID abandonment to Gaza, prisons, policing, and ecological catastrophe. Against immunity's fantasies of autonomy, purity, and self-protection, it turns to disability justice, abolitionist medicine, infectious aesthetics, and queer/crip practices of mutual aid as fugitive infrastructures of collective survival. The afterword concludes by imagining afterworlds of care: unfinished, insurgent forms of shared respiration that move beyond immunitary enclosure toward the downward redistribution of breath and breathing in common.

studies.title: Ginseng Guben Oral Liquid, a Chinese patent medicine, for post-COVID-19 fatigue: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
studies.authors: Dai, Liang, Kuah, Xiu Juan, Liu, Zhi-Dong, Hua, Hai-Bing et al.
studies.abstract: Fatigue is a prevalent and debilitating symptom in patients with post-COVID-19 condition, yet effective pharmacological interventions remain limited. Ginseng Guben Oral Liquid (RSGB), a modern patented Chinese herbal formula, is clinically used to treat fatigue associated with qi and yin deficiency, a pattern relevant to post-COVID-19 fatigue. However, high-quality evidence from randomized controlled trials is lacking. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of RSGB in patients with post-COVID-19 fatigue. This study was a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. A total of 264 eligible participants with post-COVID-19 fatigue and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) syndrome of qi and yin deficiency were enrolled from several clinical centers and randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either RSGB or a matched placebo (10 mL, twice daily) for 8 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up. The primary outcome was the change in points from baseline in the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (CFQ) score at week 8. Secondary outcomes included quality of life, TCM syndrome score, inflammatory markers and immune cell subsets. In the modified intention-to-treat population, no significant difference in the mean reduction in CFQ scores was observed between the RSGB and placebo groups (-16.0 ± 5.7 vs -15.4 ± 5.7, P = 0.404). No significant differences were observed in secondary outcomes. In a pre-specified exploratory subgroup analysis of participants with severe baseline fatigue (CFQ ≥ 22, n = 90), the results of the group treated with RSGB showed a greater reduction in CFQ scores compared to the placebo (-20.7 ± 5.6 vs -17.8 ± 6.0, P = 0.027), particularly in the domain of physical fatigue. The incidence of adverse events was comparable between groups, with no serious adverse events reported. RSGB did not demonstrate a significant overall benefit over placebo in the general post-COVID-19 fatigue. The potential signal of benefit observed in the severe fatigue subgroup requires prospective validation in trials specifically designed for this population. These findings highlight symptom severity as a factor for further research in stratified management approaches. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2300069518). studies.title: Liver-Related Biochemical Abnormalities and Coagulation Alterations in Long COVID: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
studies.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences
studies.authors: Almulla, Abbas F, Thipakorn, Yanin, Zhang, Yingqian, Maes, Michael
studies.abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to compare liver-related biochemical and coagulation biomarkers between individuals with Long COVID (LC) and controls. A search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, SciFinder, and Scopus was conducted from database inception to September 30, 2024. Sixty-one eligible studies, including 7172 participants, with 3404 individuals with LC and 3768 controls were identified. Among the liver-related biochemical markers, LC was associated with significantly higher alanine aminotransferase (ALT; SMD = 0.398; 95% CI: 0.118; 0.677), aspartate aminotransferase (AST; SMD = 0.352; 95% CI: 0.068; 0.637), and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT; SMD = 0.969; 95% CI: 0.194; 1.745) along with no significant changes in alkaline phosphatase and albumin. The composite liver biomarker index, based on those five markers was significantly higher among individuals with LC compared with controls, with a small effect size (SMD = 0.381; 95% CI: 0.149; 0.613). Among the complementary systemic and coagulation-related outcomes, lactate dehydrogenase activity (LDH; SMD = 0.489; 95% CI: 0.175; 0.802), prothrombin time (PT, SMD = 0.633; 95% CI: 0.077; 1.189), ferritin (SMD = 0.437; 95% CI: 0.069; 0.805), and D-dimer (SMD = 0.359; 95% CI: 0.144; 0.573) were significantly increased, whereas total protein was significantly decreased (SMD = -0.326; 95% CI: -0.631; -0.021). The present meta-analysis indicates that LC is associated with persistent abnormalities in several liver-related biochemical markers and coagulation-related outcomes. Further longitudinal studies are required to determine their clinical significance and long-term consequences.

studies.title: Psychosocial impacts of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19: insights from a longitudinal cohort.
studies.authors: Vallejos, Gerome, Kim, Carla Y, Alviz, Luisa F, Diaz-Ariza, Alexandra et al.
studies.abstract: To characterize subjective stress in a previously hospitalized Neuropsychiatric Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID-19 (NP-PASC) cohort in New York City by examining its distribution, patterns, and associations with psychosocial and cognitive measures. This longitudinal study conducted a 3-4 year follow-up of moderate to severe COVID-19 survivors with NP-PASC, using the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS), Urban Life Stress Scale (ULSS), and Everyday Discrimination Scale (EDS) to assess chronic stress. Associations with DSM-5 symptom domains, PSQI, UCLA Loneliness, ECog, and AD8 were analyzed using descriptive statistics, t-tests, ANOVA, chi-squared tests, and multivariate linear regression (p < 0.05). K-means clustering on standardized PSS scores identified PSS score strata (low, intermediate, high). All analyses were conducted in R version 4.3.2. Among 87 participants (mean age = 54, SD = 14), mean PSS scores for the low, intermediate, and high stress clusters were 7.08, 16.8, and 26.7, respectively. Higher perceived stress was associated with loneliness (β = 0.20, p < 0.001) and poor sleep (β = 0.34, p = 0.05). PSS scores increased by 2.07 points over time (p = 0.013), with greater increases among Hispanic (3.88, p = 0.026) and English-speaking (3.33, p = 0.008) participants. ULSS scores were higher among Spanish speakers (6.43, p = 0.017) and Hispanic/Other participants (9.5 vs. Black, p = 0.009). Discrimination experiences varied significantly by race, ethnicity, and language. Findings underscore the importance of integrating culturally sensitive, context-informed stress assessments into NP-PASC care to identify at-risk individuals and support recovery.

studies.title: Visual-verbal scanning and attention performance in individuals with long COVID-19-related dysautonomia.
studies.authors: González-Vides, Leonela, García-Velasco, Marta Alberquilla, Ruiz-Pomeda, Alicia, Hernández-Verdejo, Jose Luis et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID-19-related dysautonomia is associated with persistent cognitive and visual complaints, but brief clinically feasible tools for characterizing visual-attentional performance are needed. In this case-control study, 48 individuals with long COVID-19-related dysautonomia and 30 healthy controls completed the Modified Adult Developmental Eye Movement Test (ADEM-d), a timed visual-verbal reading/scanning task that requires sequential saccadic deployment, and the Continuous Visual Attention Test (CVAT). Compared with controls, the study group showed longer adjusted horizontal (median 73.63 vs. 54.69 s), vertical (66.35 vs. 50.66 s), and distractor (83.97 vs. 64.55 s) reading times (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001; rank-biserial r = 0.58-0.60), whereas the horizontal/vertical ratio did not differ significantly (p = 0.108). On the CVAT, the study group showed longer reaction time (378.5 vs. 320.0 ms; Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), greater reaction-time variability (96.0 vs. 62.5 ms; p = 0.001), and more omission errors (p = 0.028). Across the full sample, distractor-condition ADEM-d time was positively associated with omission errors, reaction time, and reaction-time variability (Spearman rho = 0.55-0.58; all p < 0.001). These findings indicate altered functional visual-verbal scanning and visual-attentional performance in this cohort. Because the ADEM-d does not directly record eye movements, the results do not demonstrate a primary saccadic motor deficit; additionally, the absence of a long-COVID group without dysautonomia prevents attribution of the findings specifically to dysautonomia. The ADEM-d and CVAT may nevertheless provide brief screening information to identify individuals who require more detailed visual, oculomotor, or neuropsychological assessment.

studies.title: Low-dose aripiprazole for long COVID symptom management: A retrospective observational study.
studies.authors: Cui, Jason Lunzhe, Kalaycioglu, Muge, Ricciardiello Mejia, Giorgio Camillo, Tian, Lu et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) is defined as the persistence of new or worsened symptoms for 3 or more months following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, affecting multiple organ systems. Currently, there are no approved drugs for treating LC. We reported the effect of low-dose Aripiprazole (LDA) on the management of LC symptoms in a retrospective study. A retrospective study was done using electronic health records from 50 adult patients from the Stanford LC clinic with a history of SARS-CoV-2 and subsequent LC who received LDA between 5/2021 and 10/2023. LDA was prescribed with dose titration (0.1-2.0 mg oral daily). The assessment include 29 symptoms, (ii) severity of each symptom on the Likert-scale 1 (mild) to 5 (very severe), and (iii) the Functional Status Scale (FSS) from asymptomatic (level I), symptomatic without limitations (level II), symptomatic with reduced daily activity (level III), symptomatic with a struggle to perform daily activities (level IV), or incapacitated and bedridden (level V). An improvement was defined as a reduction in the ordinal scale (V, IV, III, II, and I) from higher to lower before and after exposure to LDA. A composite score of the severity of the seven most common symptoms (headache, fatigue, brain fog, unrefreshing sleep, sleep difficulty, post-exertional malaise, and lightheadedness) was calculated to assess the effect of LDA pre- and post-treatment, using Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Tests. Within the cohort of 50 patients, the median patient age was 46.5 years, 62% were female, and the mean body mass index (BMI) was 27.5 kg/m In our cohort study, LDA was associated with improved FSS. These retrospective observational results suggest that LDA warrants further investigation in a randomized controlled trial as a therapeutic option for LC. Exploring the mechanism of action for LDA in LC may also provide new insights into pathogenesis.

studies.title: Predictors of Long COVID in Adults With Untreated Mild-to-Moderate Coronavirus Disease 2019.
studies.authors: Evering, Teresa H, Saha, Pooja T, Moser, Carlee, Jilg, Nikolaus et al.
studies.abstract: We evaluated risk factors for long COVID (LC) in the ACTIV-2/A5401 trial, with a focus on understanding the impact of sex. Findings were analyzed in nonhospitalized adults with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) receiving placebo within 10 days of symptoms. LC was defined as self-reporting COVID-19-related symptoms at study week 24 in a diary. Demographics and clinical variables, nasal viral RNA (vRNA), and inflammatory/coagulation markers were evaluated as predictors of LC, using modified Poisson regression models. Among 545 participants enrolled in January-August 2021 with a week 24 diary, the median age at entry was 44 years, 53% were female, 13% Black, 53% Hispanic/Latino, 83% US enrolled, 15% vaccinated, and 52% severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) seropositive. Seventy-four (14%) had LC (19% of female and 7% of male participants). Female sex was strongly associated with LC (adjusted risk ratio, 2.64 [95% confidence interval, 1.58-4.42]). Other predictors included US enrollment, higher total symptom score at entry, presence of symptoms at the end of the acute period (days 22-28), 28-day area under the curve of vRNA levels, and higher day 28 C-reactive protein and fibrinogen. The effect of sex persisted with adjustment for the other variables, and associations with symptoms and fibrinogen level varied by sex. In untreated adults with COVID-19, female sex, US enrollment, symptom and vRNA burden, and inflammatory/coagulation measures were associated with increased LC risk, with some associations varying by sex. The association with female sex was not significantly attenuated by adjustment for the assessed biomarkers. These data support sex-stratified investigations of LC, as well as a potential role of thromboinflammation. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04518410.

studies.title: Associations between substance use and symptomatic Long COVID in the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)-adult cohort study.
studies.authors: Okafor, Chukwuemeka N, Peterson, Ryan, Nepple, Cecilia, Jolley, Sarah et al.
studies.abstract: To determine whether frequency of tobacco, cannabis and binge alcohol use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 test result or COVID-19 symptom onset is associated with (1) presence of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and (2) development of symptomatic Long COVID over 12 months of follow-up, among those without Long COVID at study entry. Prospective cohort study with cross-sectional and longitudinal components. Multi-site study conducted across 83 clinical sites in the United States. A total of 9477 adults enrolled between October 2021 and July 2024 (median age 43 years; 74% female). Self-reported frequency of tobacco product, cannabis and binge alcohol use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 test infection (never, monthly or less, weekly or none). Symptomatic Long COVID was defined using the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)-Adult Long COVID Research Index, with scores ≥ 11 classified as symptomatic Long COVID and lower scores classified as indeterminate. Covariates included sociodemographic characteristics, clinical comorbidities and COVID-19 related factors. At study entry 20% of participants met criteria for symptomatic Long COVID. In the 12 months preceding infection, 14%, 21% and 38% reported any tobacco product, cannabis or binge alcohol use. At study entry, compared with no use, weekly or more tobacco use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID [adjusted odds ratio (aOR) = 1.37, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.13-1.67]; weekly or more cannabis use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID (aOR = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.00-1.52); and weekly or more binge alcohol use was associated with lower odds (aOR = 0.73, 95% CI = 0.58-0.91) of symptomatic Long COVID. Monthly or less use of any substance was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at study entry. Among participants without symptomatic Long COVID at study entry, weekly or more tobacco use, compared with no use, was associated with higher odds of developing symptomatic Long COVID over 12 months of follow-up (aOR = 1.29, 95% CI = 1.03-1.62). Neither cannabis nor binge alcohol use was statistically significantly associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12-month follow-up. Among adult participants of the Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER) study, weekly or more tobacco use in the 12 months prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and at 12 months among participants who did not meet criteria for symptomatic Long COVID at study entry. Weekly or more cannabis use was associated with higher odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12 months. Weekly or more binge alcohol use was associated with lower odds of symptomatic Long COVID at study entry and was not associated with symptomatic Long COVID at 12 months.

studies.title: Through the Long COVID Looking-Glass: An Unremitting Conundrum of Mitochondria?
studies.authors: Kononova, Svetlana, Bobkova, Natalia, Leonov, Sergey, Sukhikh, Gennadiy
studies.abstract: Plentiful data indicate a high post-COVID risk of developing pathologies that are long-term and result from disruption of multiple cellular processes. The significance of this data becomes increasingly clear as it links the pandemic's effects to enduring health problems which could affect millions. These conditions are usually caused by different problems with mitochondria. These problems can include less efficient energy production and increased removal of damaged cells, showing how complex cell health is. Having other health problems such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, brain diseases, and cancer related to renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) imbalance worsened COVID-19 and its lasting effects. This highlights the importance of focused treatments for these at-risk groups. This review seeks to evaluate the information on this issue, carefully studying the features and symptoms often associated with mitochondrial disorders. What happens next in the pandemic is still to be seen, but we know there is much to learn. It is important to lessen the effects of the pandemic on people with comorbidities as much as possible.

studies.title: Systemic influences on blood-brain barrier integrity - narrative review of insights from MRI.
studies.authors: Verstappen, Damon, de Jong, Joost J A, Staals, Julie, Jansen, Jacobus F A et al.
studies.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is vital for protecting the vulnerable neuronal microenvironment from harmful biomolecules. MRI is increasingly used to assess in vivo BBB integrity in various brain disorders. Thus far, extracerebral conditions that perturb the BBB via systemic pathways have received little attention. This narrative review synthesizes the available evidence for these extracerebral and systemic effects, focusing on human in vivo MRI measurements of BBB permeability. The most direct reproducible human evidence of BBB impairment was found in hypertension. Moderate evidence supports BBB involvement in systemic lupus erythematosus and long COVID. There is additionally suggestive evidence for an association with Sjögren's syndrome, HIV infection, diabetes, cardiac surgery (transient), and after pre-eclampsia. Evidence for BBB disruption is inconclusive for conditions like obstructive sleep apnea, sepsis, hyperlipidemia, obesity, alcohol abuse, and for smoking. In general, systemic inflammation emerges as a common mechanistic pathway that leads to BBB disruption and represents a target with therapeutic potential. Inflammation is amplified by a vicious cycle in which endothelial dysfunction and oxidative/metabolic stress further reinforce inflammatory signaling. Angiogenic factors also likely contribute in a subset of conditions. Heterogeneity in imaging and modeling methods and probed BBB transport pathways limits cross-study comparability. Furthermore, inherent confounding factors limit the power to detect subtle effects. Large-scale DCE-MRI studies are needed to be able to robustly map the influence of various extracerebral conditions on BBB integrity.

studies.title: Personalized cognitive and physical Telerehabilitation in post-COVID-19 condition and ME/CFS: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
studies.authors: Azcue, N, Barranco-Cano, C, Tijero-Merino, B, Acera, M et al.
studies.abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) and post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) share fatigue, post-exertional symptom exacerbation, and cognitive impairment. To explore preliminary effects and feasibility of personalized telerehabilitation in PCC and ME/CFS. This pilot randomized controlled trial analyzed 79 participants with baseline and 16-week assessments: 46 intervention and 33 standard-care controls. Individualized asynchronous cognitive and motor training was prescribed four times weekly and adapted weekly. Outcomes included neuropsychological performance, self-reported symptoms, and six-minute walk test performance. Feasibility measures included platform-recorded adherence and System Usability Scale (SUS) scores. Between-group change comparisons and domain-level Time × Group interactions were not significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Within-intervention improvements in sustained attention and semantic verbal fluency remained significant after FDR correction (both pFDR = 0.028). Exploratory principal component analysis identified PC1, explaining 27.2% of cognitive change variance. Covariate-adjusted regressions showed higher PC1 scores in intervention participants (β = 0.715, p = 0.043) and a positive association with motor adherence within this group (β = 0.089, p = 0.005); these p-values were not corrected for multiple comparisons. Median motor and cognitive adherence were 99.75% and 100.00%, respectively; median SUS was 77.5. Recorded adherence and usability provided preliminary support for feasibility under individualized clinical support, whose contact intensity was not systematically recorded. Domain-level analyses did not establish differential cognitive benefit after FDR correction. Exploratory PCA findings require confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials.

studies.title: Self-Reported Clinician Confidence in and Familiarity With Long COVID Care Following Continuing Medical Education Webinars: Unmatched Pre-Post Study.
studies.authors: Xin, Vincent Zhong, Kling, Samantha M R, Hosakote, Sindhushree, Adewuya, Ruth et al.
studies.abstract: An estimated 18-23 million Americans have had long COVID (LC), yet 54% and 72% of US physicians reported not being confident in diagnosing and treating LC, respectively. Continuing medical education (CME) is crucial to maintaining and improving clinical skills, and CME that incorporates need-based educational methods is associated with improved patient outcomes. Given limited clinician familiarity with LC, there is a need for an effective, widely accessible LC CME program. This study assessed the effectiveness of 2 Stanford University-organized LC CME webinars, which aimed to provide comprehensive, up-to-date evaluation and management strategies through multidisciplinary didactic presentations and question-and-answer sessions. Data from webinar attendees were collected through CME registration and prewebinar/postwebinar surveys. Registration surveys consisted of multiple-choice questions on profession, practice setting, experience treating vulnerable populations, and perception of LC. Prewebinar/postwebinar surveys consisted of multiple-choice questions on perception of LC, confidence in diagnosing LC, and familiarity with LC care. Prewebinar/postwebinar responses were compared using logistic regression, with Bonferroni adjustment to account for multiple testing. Statistical significance was defined as The August 2024 webinar had 449 registrants: 48.6% (n=218) were physicians, and 29.0% (n=130) reported an affiliation with an academic medical center. The attendee count was 248, with 116 and 90 attendees completing the prewebinar and postwebinar surveys, respectively. The proportion of respondents indicating that LC is a very or somewhat serious problem did not significantly differ between the pre-CME (93/115, 80.9%) and post-CME (75/88, 85.2%) surveys (adjusted CME participation was associated with significant increases in the proportions of respondents reporting confidence in diagnosing LC and familiarity with LC care, highlighting the potential of virtual CME programs to support clinician education.

studies.title: Comprehensive Immunogenetic Analysis of Long COVID Reveals HLA-B*15 as an Independent Protective Factor.
studies.authors: Cano-Perales, José Luis, Ortuño Pastor, Pedro José, Rosales-Castillo, Antonio, Bernal, Mónica et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a frequent complication of SARS-CoV-2 infection, but the contribution of host immunogenetic factors to its development remains poorly understood. We investigated the association of HLA polymorphisms and other immunogenetic markers with Long COVID in a Spanish cohort. We performed a case-control study including 453 hospitalised patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, of whom 168 developed Long COVID and 959 healthy controls. High-resolution HLA typing was performed together with analyses of conserved extended haplotypes (CEHs), HLA-B Bw4/Bw6 epitopes, HLA-C C1/C2 ligand groups, MICA short tandem repeat polymorphisms and the CCR5 Δ32 variant. Logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of Long COVID. After correction for multiple testing, no high-resolution HLA allele remained significantly associated with Long COVID. However, the low-resolution HLA-B*15 serotype was significantly less frequent in patients with Long COVID and remained independently associated with a reduced risk of persistent symptoms after adjustment for age, sex and intensive care unit admission. The conserved extended haplotype CEH 44.2 was also less frequent among patients with Long COVID, although this association was not retained after multivariable adjustment. No significant associations were observed for HLA-B Bw4/Bw6 epitopes, HLA-C C1/C2 ligand groups, MICA polymorphisms or the CCR5 Δ32 variant. Our findings identify HLA-B*15 as an independent protective immunogenetic factor against Long COVID and support a role for HLA-mediated antiviral immunity in modulating susceptibility to persistent post-COVID manifestations. These results warrant validation in larger, independent cohorts.

studies.title: Neuropsychiatric long COVID is associated with altered SARS-CoV-2-specific cellular-humoral coordination and diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity up to 12 months post-COVID-19 symptom onset.
studies.authors: Samaan, Philip, Budylowski, Patrick, Matveev, Vitaliy, Russell, Victoria et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a chronic multisystemic condition estimated to affect approximately 400 million people worldwide. Although underlying mechanisms remain elusive, persistent SARS-CoV-2 reservoirs and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) reactivation have been implicated. We compared SARS-CoV-2- and EBV-specific cellular and humoral immunity between 27 long COVID individuals with ≥2 neuropsychiatric symptoms and 27 matched recovered participants at 3-6 months post-COVID-19 symptom onset (PSO). Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were assessed for IFN-γ, IL-2, TNF, and granzyme B T-cell responses against SARS-CoV-2, EBV, and HCMV. Sera were evaluated for neutralizing activity against live ancestral SARS-CoV-2 and EBV, while EBV reactivation was assessed by anti-early antigen-diffuse IgG and anti-viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM. We observed no significant differences in SARS-CoV-2-, EBV-, or HCMV-specific Th1-type/cytotoxic T-cell responses or live virus neutralization between long COVID and recovered groups at 3-6 months PSO. Although SARS-CoV-2-specific IFN-γ and IL-2 T-cell responses correlated with serological neutralizing capacity in recovered participants, no such associations were observed in the long COVID group, suggesting altered coordination between cellular and humoral immunity. EBV reactivation was only detected in one neuropsychiatric long COVID participant. However, EBV anti-VCA IgG antibody levels were significantly diminished in long COVID participants at 3-6 months PSO. Reports of fatigue at 12 months PSO were also associated with reduced EBV neutralizing capacity at 3-6 months PSO. Diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity and dysregulated coordination between SARS-CoV-2-specific cellular and humoral immunity may thus represent potential prognostic markers for neuropsychiatric long COVID development and fatigue up to 12 months PSO.IMPORTANCEWe performed a comprehensive analysis of cellular and humoral immune responses to SARS-CoV-2, Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), and human cytomegalovirus in individuals with neuropsychiatric long COVID, a subgroup that remains poorly characterized. Although no differences in virus-specific Th1-type or cytotoxic T-cell immunity were observed between individuals with long COVID and recovered individuals, altered coordination between SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell and neutralizing humoral immunity was observed in the long COVID group at 3-6 months post-COVID-19 symptom onset (PSO). Diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity was also associated with neuropsychiatric long COVID and fatigue up to 12 months PSO. Together, these findings suggest that altered SARS-CoV-2-specific cellular-humoral immune coordination and diminished EBV-specific humoral immunity may contribute to the development or persistence of neuropsychiatric long COVID and highlight a promising future direction for mechanistic studies.CLINICAL TRIALSThis study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov as NCT05125510.

studies.title: Obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID syndrome: a scoping review of current evidence in adults.
studies.authors: Alhotye, Munyra I, Alotaibi, Tareq F, Alotaibi, Manar M, Alojyri, Renad M et al.
studies.abstract: Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep disorder characterized by intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation, contributing to systemic inflammation and autonomic dysfunction. Long COVID refers to persistent symptoms following acute COVID-19 infection. Emerging evidence suggests an association between OSA and persistent post-COVID-19 symptoms, potentially mediated by overlapping biological pathways; however, the direction and causality of this relationship remain uncertain. This scoping review aimed to examine the current evidence regarding the different associations between OSA and Long COVID in adults, summarize the reported clinical findings, and explore the proposed pathophysiological mechanisms linking OSA and Long COVID. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for studies published between 2020 and 2026. Eligible studies included observational studies, clinical trials, and reviews involving adults with OSAand/or Long COVID syndrome. Two independent reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and synthesized findings thematically. Of 184 identified records, 11 studies met the inclusion criteria. Evidence suggested different associations between OSA and Long COVID across the included studies. Proposed mechanisms included intermittent hypoxia, systemic inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, sleep fragmentation, and circadian disturbance; however, these mechanisms were not consistently measured across studies. Reported Long COVID manifestations among patients with OSA included fatigue, respiratory impairment, cognitive dysfunction, and cardiovascular complications. Evidence regarding the impact of OSA treatment on Long COVID outcomes was limited. Current evidence suggests an association between OSA and Long COVID, although the nature and direction of this association vary across studies. However, the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify this relationship and determine whether effective OSA management can improve Long COVID outcomes.

studies.title: Age-related differences in long COVID symptoms and outcomes: a cross-sectional study in Jordan.
studies.authors: Shaltaf, Enas Hussien, Mat, Sumaiyah, Azmi, Nor Azura, Alghwiri, Alia et al.
studies.abstract: Long coronavirus disease (COVID) causes persistent physical, psychological, and functional symptoms. This study compared symptom prevalence and outcomes between younger (<60 years) and older (≥60 years) Jordanian adults with long COVID. This cross-sectional study included adults with polymerase chain reaction-confirmed coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and symptoms persisting ≥2 months. An Arabic questionnaire was administered online or by telephone. Fatigue, functional status, dyspnea, and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Fatigue Severity Scale, Post-COVID-19 Functional Status (PCFS) scale, modified Medical Research Council scale, and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Group comparisons and multivariable logistic regression were performed, adjusting for sex, smoking, comorbidity, and vaccination. Among 938 participants, 596 (63.5%) were younger than 60 years. Fatigue was common in both groups (93.3% vs. 90.6%; P=0.143). Younger adults reported more dyspnea, muscle pain, dizziness, anxiety/depression, and brain fog (all P<0.05). Older adults had more severe functional limitation (PCFS grade 4: 24.6% vs. 16.1%; P=0.002) and greater depressive symptom severity (P=0.029). After adjustment, younger age was associated with lower odds of moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.624; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.468-0.830; P=0.001), but not with severe functional limitation (aOR, 1.340; 95% CI, 0.949-1.891; P=0.096). Younger adults reported a broader range of symptoms, whereas older adults experienced greater functional impairment and depressive symptom severity. Age remained independently associated with depressive symptoms but not severe functional limitation.

studies.title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis in Post-COVID condition symptoms: relation with chronic fatigue and functional limitation.
studies.authors: Carpallo-Porcar, Beatriz, García-Martínez, Laura, Jiménez-Sánchez, Carolina, Calvo, Sandra et al.
studies.abstract: Post-COVID Condition (PCC) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which chronic fatigue and functional limitation are among the most disabling manifestations. Alterations in the gut microbiota have been proposed as contributors to PCC pathophysiology; however, it remains unclear whether distinct clinical PCC phenotypes are associated with specific microbiota signatures. This cross-sectional pilot study analysed gut microbiota composition and predicted functional capacity in 50 participants from Aragón (Spain), including 30 patients with PCC and 20 healthy controls. PCC patients were stratified according to the presence of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS)-like symptoms and functional limitation assessed using the 6-Minute Walking Test. Alpha and beta diversity did not differ significantly between groups (Figs. 2 and 3). Differential abundance analysis identified taxon-level differences between groups. Escherichia/Shigella was enriched in PCC-CFS relative to controls, both overall and in the subgroup without functional limitation, representing the most consistent signal. Additional differences included higher Streptococcus and Veillonella in controls, and higher Flavonifractor and Hungatella in PCC-NCFS. After adjustment for digestive symptoms and vaccine dose, these associations attenuated and none remained significant, indicating that they may be partly driven by confounding.PICRUSt2 functional predictions suggested differences in pathways related to nucleotide and amino acid metabolism; however, none remained significant after correction for multiple testing and should therefore be considered exploratory. These findings suggest the presence of phenotype-associated taxonomic differences within PCC despite the absence of global diversity alterations. The results should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating due to the limited subgroup sample sizes. Larger studies incorporating metagenomic and metabolomic approaches are needed to validate these observations and clarify their potential clinical relevance.

studies.title: Prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation combined with cognitive training reduces anxiety, daytime sleepiness, and cognitive complaints in women after COVID-19: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
studies.authors: Soares, Beatriz Marcelle Vieira, Coelho, Luiza Chaga, Bonfim, Arthur Dutra do, Bueno, Guilherme Augusto Santos
studies.abstract: Persistent anxiety, disturbed sleep, and subjective cognitive complaints are frequent and often co-occur after COVID-19, especially in women, yet interventions addressing them together are limited. We examined whether adding left-prefrontal transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to cognitive training reduces these symptoms in women with post-COVID cognitive complaints. In a single-centre, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial, 30 women with confirmed prior COVID-19 and self-reported cognitive decline (Mini-Mental State Examination ≥ 24; no diagnosed neurodegenerative disorder) were allocated to three groups (n = 10 each): cognitive training plus active tDCS (CT + tDCS), cognitive training plus sham tDCS (CT + sham), or cognitive training only (CT only). Active tDCS targeted the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (2 mA, 20 min; anode F3, return F7) across nine sessions over three weeks. Anxiety (Beck Anxiety Inventory), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), cognition (Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination-Revised), reaction times (psychomotor speed), and prefrontal electroencephalographic (EEG) cortical arousal and frontal asymmetry were assessed at baseline and after the ninth session; there was no follow-up. All participants completed the trial (no dropout). Groups were compared using analysis of covariance adjusted for the corresponding baseline score, with non-parametric confirmation and false-discovery-rate correction. Relative to both comparison groups, the CT + tDCS group showed significantly lower anxiety and daytime sleepiness and higher global cognition, memory, and fluency, with faster reaction times (all corrected p < .05). Cortical arousal increased and frontal asymmetry shifted toward greater relative left-frontal activation. The CT + sham and CT only groups did not differ from each other, and near-ceiling attention and visuospatial scores were unchanged. Adding left-prefrontal tDCS to cognitive training reduced anxiety and daytime sleepiness and improved cognition and psychomotor speed in women with post-COVID cognitive complaints, with parallel changes in prefrontal EEG markers. Confirmation in larger samples is needed.

studies.title: Web-Based Isha Kriya Meditation and Breathwork in Long COVID: Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Pilot Study.
studies.authors: Rayapuraju, Akila, Mohamed, Enas, Reed, Preeti Upadhyay, Orui, Hibiki et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID affects millions of adults, causing fatigue, dyspnea, cognitive symptoms, and mood disturbances. Effective treatments are limited, and many patients cannot access multidisciplinary rehabilitation because of symptom fluctuation, distance, or specialist shortages. Web-based mind-body interventions may offer accessible, scalable support alongside existing care. We assessed the feasibility and efficacy of a 3-week web-based yogic breathing and meditation program for long COVID symptoms. In this completed, parallel-group, 6-week waitlist-controlled, mixed methods randomized trial, adults aged 18-70 years with physician-confirmed long COVID were recruited from US clinics and self-referral and randomized 1:1 to immediate intervention or waitlist control, crossing over at week 3. The program included live webinars and video guides for daily self-practice. The primary outcome was adherence, defined as practicing at least 1 of 3 techniques on ≥4 days/week across all 3 active-intervention weeks. Secondary outcomes included perceived stressmood, quality of life, dyspnea, and somatic symptom burden, assessed at baseline, 3 weeks, and 6 weeks. Quantitative outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Semistructured interviews and focus groups underwent conventional content analysis and were integrated with quantitative findings via joint display. Of 189 randomized participants, 1 was excluded post-randomization for a protocol deviation; 188 (96 intervention, 92 waitlist) began the study. Of these, 124 reached the active intervention period. Among 58 with complete adherence data, 55% met the adherence threshold (60% intervention, 50% waitlist). Secondary analyses included 185 participants with ≥1 assessment. No adverse events were reported. Compared with waitlist control, the intervention group showed greater reductions in total mood disturbance (MD=-10; 95% CI -19 to -1.6; P=.02), negative mood (MD=-7.5; 95% CI -15 to -0.44; P=.04), fatigue (MD=-2.9; 95% CI -4.6 to -1.2; P=.001), MDP immediate perception (MD=-5.5; 95% CI -9.4 to -1.6; P=.007), MDP sensory dimension (MD=-5.1; 95% CI -8.5 to -1.7; P=.003), and somatic symptom burden (MD=-2.0; 95% CI -3.6 to -0.38; P=.02), and greater increases in positive mood (MD=2.9; 95% CI 0.66 to 5.1; P=.01) and vigor (MD=1.7; 95% CI 0.18 to 3.2; P=.03). Stress and quality of life did not differ significantly. Qualitative findings identified medical-system struggles, digital delivery, online support, and practices' effects on resilience and identity. Integration showed convergence for dyspnea and mood, divergence for stress and quality of life, and expansion through themes of medical-system experience, identity, and social connection. This web-based yogic breathing and meditation program appears feasible and accessible for people with long COVID. By combining 3 practices in a brief protocol and integrating quantitative and qualitative evidence, this study provides novel insight into both symptom outcomes and dimensions of recovery not captured by standardized measures. Further evaluation should assess longer-term effects and integration into scalable telehealth and virtual rehabilitation pathways.

studies.title: Mind-body reprogramming therapy: development, theoretical foundation, and clinical application for Long COVID.
studies.authors: Jacobsen, Henrik Børsting, Reme, Silje Endresen
studies.abstract: This paper presents the development and clinical rationale for Mind-Body Reprogramming Therapy (MBRT), a novel, theory-based intervention for patients with Long COVID experiencing persistent symptoms. Rooted in predictive processing, classical and operant conditioning, and Relational Frame Theory (RFT), MBRT targets maladaptive brain-based alarm responses believed to underlie symptoms such as fatigue, pain, and cognitive dysfunction. We argue that the chronicity of these alarms in patients reflects not only inferential biases and conditioned responses, but verbal relational networks that bind symptoms to identity, anticipated futures, and rule-governed avoidance, which become primary targets of treatment. The intervention combines personalized education, stress regulation techniques, and experiential learning delivered by an interdisciplinary team over a 7-10-day hybrid format. We describe the theoretical foundation of MBRT and outline its core components, including psychoeducation, values clarification, interoceptive exposure, and behavior change strategies. A detailed case study illustrates the therapeutic process and potential for recovery. We argue that persistent symptoms in Long COVID may reflect learned brain patterns rather than ongoing physical injury, and that targeted interdisciplinary interventions can help patients reverse these patterns. MBRT is currently under evaluation in a randomized controlled trial.

studies.title: Effectiveness of an Extension for Community Health Outcomes case-based virtual community of practice model on patient outcomes for the management of long COVID and other fatiguing illnesses: a randomized control trial.
studies.authors: Sharp, Sydney P, Zhang, Tianmai M, Taren, Douglas, Zuber, Alexandra et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a heterogeneous chronic condition with symptoms that often overlap with other infection-associated chronic conditions (IACC). These clinical similarities highlight gaps in healthcare education and delivery, leaving many primary care clinicians unprepared to manage these conditions. To address this need, we conducted a two-arm, single-blind, cluster randomized controlled trial (Clinicaltrials.gov ID NCT05167227) in an under-resourced Federally Qualified Health Center primary care setting to evaluate the effectiveness of the Long COVID and Fatiguing Illness Recovery Program in improving patient outcomes with long COVID, myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, and other IACCs. From December 2021 through October 2023, 20 primary care clinicians were randomized in a 1:1 ratio. The intervention arm participated in weekly multidisciplinary Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes (ECHO) case-based virtual community of practice sessions, monthly webinars, and quarterly short courses. The control arm participated in monthly webinars and quarterly short courses. A total of 590 patients were assigned to participating clinicians and completed surveys including Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS)-29 at baseline, 3-, 6-, 9-, and 12-months. Patient-reported outcomes from 298 control and 289 intervention patients completed surveys were analyzed using statistical tests and linear mixed-effects regression to examine between-arm differences and longitudinal treatment effects. Both arms showed improvements over 12 months on multiple PROMIS scales including Fatigue, Physical Function, Pain Interference, Social Roles, Dyspnea, and Applied Cognition, approaching reference population norms at study end. A statistically significant difference was observed on pain interference, with the intervention arm having better outcomes than control at 12 months [mean (SD): 57 (11) vs. 60 (10), The ECHO case-based virtual community of practice model showed evidence that clinician-focused education may enhance primary care management of patients with complex fatiguing illnesses, supporting the model's value in under-resourced settings.

studies.title: Canadian guidelines for post COVID-19 condition (CAN-PCC): A summary for general practitioners.
studies.journal: The European journal of general practice
studies.authors: Aloosh, Mehdi, Hopkins, Jessica P, Nieuwlaat, Robby, Darzi, Andrea J et al.
studies.abstract: Post COVID-19 condition (PCC), also known as Long COVID is associated with a substantial global burden. The Canadian Guidelines for Post COVID-19 Condition (CAN-PCC), developed by the CAN-PCC Collaborative, led by McMaster University's Cochrane Canada and GRADE Centres with support from the Public Health Agency of Canada, synthesised over 100 recommendations across prevention, diagnosis, clinical interventions and individualised care, neurological and psychiatric care, paediatric considerations, and health system supports. This summary highlights key, actionable recommendations for general practitioners and outlines their relevance across diverse healthcare contexts. We extracted recommendations from the CAN‑PCC guidelines and organized them into four domains. Across the four domains, several priority recommendations for general practitioners were identified: [1] testing, identification and diagnosis (conditional recommendation for symptom‑guided work‑up; strong recommendation to screen adults for depression); [2] clinical interventions (conditional recommendation for patient‑centred goals, functional recovery, targeted pharmacotherapy, and non-pharmacological strategies); [3] prevention (conditional recommendation for vaccination, masking, indoor air quality improvement, early outpatient pharmacotherapy where indicated, including metformin and nirmatrelvir/ritonavir); and [4] paediatric considerations (conditional recommendation for vaccination and mental‑health screening; strong recommendation against cannabidiol/CBD). As evidence evolves, the CAN‑PCC guidelines provide a comprehensive, patient‑centred framework to support general practitioners in the prevention, identification, and management of PCC. Its recommendations can be adapted across varied healthcare settings to support consistent, safe, and effective care delivery. Diagnosis of post-COVID-19 condition (PCC) requires a symptom‑guided assessment to exclude alternative conditions and identify functional impact.Management of PCC focuses on patient‑centred, multidisciplinary strategies that support symptom relief, functional recovery, and safe, individualized pacing.Prevention of PCC relies on vaccination, masking, and improved indoor air quality, with early outpatient pharmacotherapy reducing risk after infection.

studies.title: Association between physical activity before SARS-CoV-2 infection and functional disability 24 months after COVID-19: findings from the SulCOVID-19 longitudinal study.
studies.authors: Dos Santos Afonso, Max, Vieira, Yohana Pereira, Rocha, Juliana Quadros Santos, Duro, Suele Manjourany Silva et al.
studies.abstract: Individuals diagnosed with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), even those with mild illness, report persistent fatigue, muscle weakness, and worsening functionality in the activities of daily living. Individuals who engaged in regular physical activity before infection with the causative agent, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), reportedly exhibited greater resilience to negative COVID-19 outcomes. Therefore, this study evaluated the association between physical activity before SARS-CoV-2 infection and functional disability 24 months after COVID-19. This longitudinal study was based on the SulCovid-19 survey and used the Lawton and Brody scale to measure functional disability. Physical activity was assessed based on frequency (days per week) and duration (time per day) and categorized according to the WHO recommendation of ≥ 150 min/week.Control variables included sex, age, skin color, annual income, body mass index, morbidity, and hospitalization. Poisson regression analysis with robust variance adjustment was performed to calculate prevalence ratios and corresponding 95% confidence intervals. Individuals who engaged in physical activity before acute SARS-CoV-2 infection had a 20% lower prevalence of disability in instrumental activities of daily living 24 months after infection (adjusted PR 0.80; 95% CI 0.66-0.98). Physical activity before SARS-CoV-2 infection was associated with a lower prevalence of disability in instrumental activities of daily living 24 months after COVID-19.

studies.title: A central hub model for remote delivery of multisite clinical trial interventions.
studies.authors: Charvet, Leigh, Pilloni, Giuseppina, Becker, Jacqueline H, Wisnivesky, Juan et al.
studies.abstract: Digital health technologies enable remote delivery of clinical interventions, creating opportunities to redesign multisite trials. Traditional trials require participating sites to deliver interventions independently, potentially increasing implementation variability and operational complexity. Centralized models instead allow local recruitment and assessments while coordinating intervention delivery through one hub. We describe the feasibility of this model in RECOVER-NEURO, an NIH-funded, five-arm phase 2 randomized trial overseen by the Duke Clinical Research Institute. The trial enrolled 328 participants across 22 US sites with cognitive symptoms associated with long COVID. Sites conducted recruitment, consent, and clinical assessments, while an NYU Langone Health hub managed study kit preparation and distribution, device programming, onboarding, remote supervision, adherence monitoring, and equipment recovery. Participants were randomized to BrainHQ cognitive training alone; BrainHQ plus cognitive rehabilitation (PASC-CoRE), delivered via telehealth by Mount Sinai and Emory University investigators; BrainHQ plus active transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS); BrainHQ plus sham tDCS; or non-adaptive computer-based puzzles and games as an active comparator. Interventions were delivered remotely over 10 weeks using home-based study kits. Participants completed a mean of 44.0 ± 10.9 sessions over 68.8 ± 11.3 days. Of 320 participants who received intervention, 260 (81.3%) were consistently adherent. The hub initiated intervention within 13.5 ± 6.1 days of first participant contact, supported up to 168 concurrently active participants, and achieved a 96.9% equipment return rate. The intervention phase was completed in 375 days. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of centralized remote delivery of digital and device-based interventions in a large multisite trial and may inform future decentralized or hybrid clinical trials. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05965739.

studies.title: Examining the Feasibility, Acceptability, and Preliminary Efficacy of a Health App for Postacute Pandemic Years in Managing Physical and Psychological Distress Symptoms: Pilot Quasi-Experimental Study.
studies.authors: Liu, Justina Yat Wa, Man, David, Lai, Frank Ho Yin, Wong, Rina Wing Yan et al.
studies.abstract: Physical and psychological distress symptoms can adversely affect daily functioning and quality of life, highlighting the need for accessible self-management support. Although mobile health (mHealth) interventions show promise in supporting physical symptom management, evidence regarding their feasibility and potential effects on psychological distress remains limited. This pilot study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of the health app for postacute pandemic years (HAPPY) for managing physical and psychological distress symptoms. A 2-arm, single-blind, quasi-experimental trial was conducted from July 2023 to January 2024. Thirty-eight participants experiencing distress symptoms related to COVID-19 were assigned to the experimental group or a waitlist control group. The experimental group received a 24-week mHealth intervention through the HAPPY app, which included an 8-week supervised phase with weekly face-to-face sessions and a 16-week self-management phase. The control group received no active treatment. Feasibility was assessed through recruitment, adherence, and adverse event monitoring, whereas preliminary efficacy was evaluated at 8 weeks (T1) and 24 weeks (T2) and compared with baseline (T0) using quantitative measures of distress, fatigue, sleep quality, pain, emotional regulation, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The study demonstrated the feasibility of the HAPPY app, with a recruitment rate of 88.37% (38/43), a dropout rate of 10.5% (4/38), and an adherence rate of 93.33% (14/15) for the supervised sessions. No adverse events were reported. Significant within-group improvements were observed for distress (Kessler Psychological Distress Scale [K10]; P<.001), fatigue (Brief Fatigue Inventory-Chinese [BFI-C]; P<.001), sleep quality (Chinese Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [CPSQI]; P=.009), and PTSD symptoms (Chinese Impact of Event Scale-Revised [CIES-R]; P=.02). However, between-group differences were limited. The study demonstrated the HAPPY app's feasibility, acceptability, and potential efficacy for managing physical and psychological distress symptoms. High recruitment, retention, and adherence rates, along with measurable improvements in distress, fatigue, sleep quality, and pain, suggest the app's promise as a scalable intervention. studies.title: Antidepressants in postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS): A scoping review.
studies.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
studies.authors: Blitshteyn, Svetlana, Reiersen, Angela M, Weinstock, Leonard B, Speed, Traci J et al.
studies.abstract: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) is one of the most common autonomic disorders with increasing prevalence and incidence after COVID-19 pandemic. Despite standard treatment of POTS consisting of nonpharmacologic and pharmacologic therapies that decrease heart rate and increase blood pressure and plasma volume, antidepressant medications are widely utilized in patients with POTS. We conducted a scoping review of literature to examine the published studies on the use of antidepressants and their efficacy in patients with POTS. We found only 2 studies, one retrospective chart review involving bupropion and second study of a randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial of a single dose of sertraline 50 mg. Both studies showed no benefits of these medications on orthostatic vital signs or orthostatic symptoms. A third study involving retrospective chart review did not examine medication efficacy, but found that nearly half of 120 patients with POTS were taking some type of antidepressant or antianxiety medication while only 15.7% were taking cardiovascular medications for treatment of POTS. Based on very limited available data, we conclude that antidepressants show no efficacy for treatment of POTS despite being widely utilized. Education of healthcare professionals regarding proper diagnosis and appropriate treatment of POTS is essential to instituting the right treatment and avoiding inappropriate use of antidepressants in this patient population.

studies.title: COVID-19 Is Not an Independent Risk Factor for Post-Intensive Care Syndrome: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
studies.authors: Antinoro, Alberto, Leder, Antonia, Grunow, Julius J, Steinecke, Karin et al.
studies.abstract: BackgroundPost-intensive care syndrome (PICS) affects many ICU survivors, leading to persistent physical, cognitive, and mental health issues. The COVID-19 pandemic raised concerns about whether SARS-CoV-2 infection increases PICS risk. This study aimed to evaluate whether COVID-19 is an independent risk factor for PICS and to identify other contributing factors.MethodsThis retrospective cohort included 92 patients treated for respiratory failure in three ICUs at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin between July 2020 and September 2021. Patients were divided into COVID-19 (n = 49) and non-COVID-19 (n = 43) groups. At three months post-discharge, outpatient assessments consisted of demographic data, ICU-related variables, and evaluations of physical (handgrip dynamometry, Timed Up and Go test), cognitive (Mini-Cog, Animal Naming Test), and psychological health (PHQ-4). PICS was defined as at least one abnormal test; severity was graded by the number of affected domains. Logistic and ordinal regression analyses assessed whether COVID-19 was independently associated with PICS prevalence and severity.ResultsPICS was present in 71.4% of COVID-19 and 62.8% of non-COVID survivors (p = 0.378). Multivariable analysis showed no significant association between COVID-19 and PICS or its severity (OR = 1.46; 95% CI 0.50-4.23; p = 0.486; and OR = 1.09; 95% CI 0.45-2.68; p = 0.845, respectively).ConclusionsCOVID-19 was not independently associated with PICS in ICU survivors. Both groups experience high rates of long-term impairments, highlighting the importance of rehabilitation and follow-up care for all ICU survivors.

studies.title: Tumor microenvironment-driven therapeutic resistance in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
studies.authors: Li, Hong-Jia, Cui, Jia-Ning, Yang, Xin, Li, Jia-Hang et al.
studies.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most treatment-refractory malignancies, with limited and often transient benefit from chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy. Therapeutic resistance is increasingly recognized as an ecosystem-level process arising from reciprocal interactions between malignant cells and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Dense extracellular matrix, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs), dysfunctional vasculature, immunosuppressive myeloid and lymphoid populations, hypoxic niches, metabolic networks, microbiota, extracellular vesicles (EVs), and neural components collectively restrict drug delivery and promote adaptive survival, immune escape, stemness, and treatment-induced evolution. This review integrates these processes into a PDAC resistance ecosystem framework. We discuss how stromal remodeling, hypoxia-driven adaptation, metabolic-immune crosstalk, extracellular communication, cancer stem cell plasticity, and TME-regulated autophagy and ferroptosis contribute to resistance across therapeutic modalities. We further evaluate emerging strategies involving stromal reprogramming, myeloid and immune remodeling, metabolic intervention, hypoxia targeting, and regulated cell-death sensitization. Particular emphasis is placed on the limited clinical translation of indiscriminate stromal depletion and single-target approaches. Finally, we propose that spatial multi-omics, longitudinal biomarker profiling, and adaptive combination therapy will be required to identify dominant resistance programs and guide patient-specific intervention in PDAC.

studies.title: Mechanistic insights and translational perspectives on liver fibrosis through single-cell transcriptomics.
studies.authors: Lu, Weiwei, Xu, Jun, Wang, Kexin, Chen, Yumu et al.
studies.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a defining feature of chronic liver diseases and can progress to cirrhosis and liver failure. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution analysis of cellular heterogeneity and multicellular interactions during fibrogenesis. In this narrative review, we analyzed published single-cell transcriptomic studies from experimental models and human cohorts, focusing on cell-type-specific programs, cell-state trajectories inferred by Monocle, and intercellular communication networks predicted using CellChat and CellPhoneDB. Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) consistently emerged as the primary extracellular matrix-producing cells, with conserved activation signatures involving collagen synthesis, Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-Protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) signaling, and matrix organization.
