studies.title: Persistent exertional dyspnea following mild COVID-19: potential association with diaphragm impairment.
studies.authors: Regmi, Binaya, Ratsimba, Sitraka Faniry Nantenaina, Jörn, Benedikt, Giannoni, Alberto et al.
studies.abstract: Persistent exertional dyspnea is a common symptom in long COVID, and routine cardiopulmonary testing is often unrevealing. The underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Although exertional dyspnea has been linked to diaphragm weakness among hospitalized individuals, studies using state-of-the-art respiratory muscle assessment in non-hospitalized cohorts are lacking. This study investigated the role of respiratory muscle function in exertional dyspnea in non-hospitalized patients after mild COVID-19 infection. 25 outpatients with persistent dyspnea were assessed at a median 24 months after mild COVID-19 infection. Evaluations included pulmonary function testing, 6-minute walk test, echocardiography, twitch transdiaphragmatic pressure (TwPdi) following cervical magnetic stimulation of the phrenic nerve roots, and diaphragm ultrasound. Diaphragm parameters were compared with those of a healthy control group (3:1 matched for age, sex, BMI, and comorbidities). Routine blood results, pulmonary function testing or echocardiography showed no clear alternative explanation for dyspnea at the group level. However, COVID-19 individuals exhibited significantly lower diaphragm strength (expressed in TwPdi) than controls (p=0.02), with results varying across dyspnea subgroups (overall ANOVA p-value = 0.009). A negative correlation was observed between TwPdi and dyspnea expressed on mBorg scale (r = -0.67, 95% CI -0.84 to -0.37, p < 0.001). Signs indicating potential structural alterations were observed in post-COVID patients, with significantly reduced diaphragm thickness at functional residual capacity (FRC) and total lung capacity (TLC) compared to controls (p = 0.02 and p < 0.001). Persistent exertional dyspnea after mild COVID-19 is associated with diaphragm weakness and structural changes despite normal cardiopulmonary findings, supporting a key role for respiratory muscle impairment as a potential contributor to dyspnea in long COVID despite initial mild infection.

studies.title: Real-world outcomes of a multidisciplinary rehabilitation programme for adults with long COVID: a retrospective cohort study.
studies.authors: Daodu, Lanre Peter, Nottingham, Kim, Raste, Yogini, Allgrove, Judith E et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID imposes a substantial and ongoing burden, with persistent symptoms affecting daily functioning and quality of life. Multidisciplinary rehabilitation has been widely implemented in clinical practice; however, evidence describing real-world patient outcomes and service delivery remains limited. This study aimed to describe clinical and patient-reported outcomes among adults participating in a structured multidisciplinary rehabilitation programme for Long COVID, and to explore the association between referral-to-assessment time and changes in outcomes. This retrospective cohort study analysed routinely collected clinical data from adult patients who completed a structured multidisciplinary rehabilitation programme at the Long COVID rehabilitation centre in a university hospital in South London (January 2021-December 2023). Seven validated outcome instruments were administered at baseline and discharge: the Work and Social Adjustment Scale (WSAS), Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS), MRC Dyspnoea Scale, Patient Health Questionnaire-2 (PHQ-2), Generalised Anxiety Disorder-2 (GAD-2), EQ-5D-5 L, and 1-minute Sit-to-Stand test (STS-1). Pre-to-post changes were assessed using paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; the proportion of patients achieving minimal clinically important differences (MCIDs) was determined for each measure. The association between referral-to-assessment time and outcome change was examined using linear correlation and restricted cubic spline (RCS) modelling. A total of 170 participants were included. Statistically significant improvements were observed across all primary domains after adjustment for multiple comparisons, except self-care and pain/discomfort. The largest effect was recorded for physical endurance (STS-1: r = 0.590, p < 0.001), followed by breathlessness (MRC: r = 0.491), fatigue (FSS: r = 0.382), and functional impairment (WSAS: d = - 0.323). MCID thresholds were achieved by 63.5% of patients on the STS-1, 48.8% for breathlessness, and 45.9% for depression. No significant linear association was identified between referral delay and outcome change. Non-linear therapeutic windows were identified in functional and psychological domains using RCS modelling. Patients assessed 100-150 days after referral showed the greatest improvement, with benefits declining thereafter. Participants demonstrated improvements in clinical and patient-reported outcomes over time during engagement in a multidisciplinary rehabilitation programme for Long COVID. While causal attribution is limited by the observational design, these findings provide real-world evidence on patient outcomes and highlight the potential importance of timely access to rehabilitation services. Further prospective and controlled studies are needed to evaluate effectiveness and optimise care pathways.

studies.title: Efficacy and Safety of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy for Fatigue and Neurocognitive Symptoms in Long COVID: A Prospective Observational Study.
studies.authors: Lee, Yujin, Chang, Jhin Goo, Lee, Kyoungmi, Kim, Inbyung et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID or post-COVID-19 condition is characterized as the continuation or development of new symptoms 3 months after the initial SARS-CoV-2 infection, with these symptoms lasting for at least 2 months with no other explanation. Fatigue and brain fog are among the most prevalent symptoms of long COVID, which significantly impact individuals' quality of life, but treatment options for these symptoms have been limited. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) is suggested as a possible treatment option for long COVID. This study aimed to investigate the effect of HBOT on fatigue and the neuropsychiatric symptoms of long COVID. This study included 49 long COVID patients with fatigue caseness, as defined by a Chalder Fatigue Scale (CFQ) bimodal score of ≥ 4. The subjects underwent 10 HBOT sessions, once daily at 2 atmospheres for 90 minutes over 12 days. The clinical outcomes were assessed using the bimodal and Likert scores of the CFQ, selected cognitive function tests, validated neuropsychological scales, and a subjective post-COVID-19 symptom checklist before and after HBOT. The adverse events were also assessed. Paired t-tests were performed, and the safety evaluations were conducted. Out of the 49 subjects included in the analyses, 37 completed the treatment. After HBOT, 36 out of 49 (73.5%) subjects recovered from fatigue (CFQ bimodal score of < 4). The overall fatigue severity significantly decreased (CFQ Likert score mean ± standard deviation, 22.67 ± 5.12 at baseline vs. 6.46 ± 7.14 post-treatment, The significant reduction in fatigue, improvements in several cognitive function domains, mental health outcomes, and post-COVID-19 symptoms suggest that HBOT could be a potential therapeutic option for long COVID. Clinical Research Information Service Identifier: KCT0008274.

studies.title: Disparities in long COVID diagnosis among a care-seeking population in the Midwestern United States: An approach to identifying underdiagnosis.
studies.authors: Rivelli, Anne, Ording, Jeffrey, Ford, Tiffany, Doll, Margaret K et al.
studies.abstract: To identify predictors of Long COVID diagnosis among patients seeking care for Long COVID symptoms to document potential underdiagnosis and diagnostic disparities. In this retrospective study using electronic health records from a midwestern healthcare system, we identified adults with SARS-CoV-2 between July 1, 2021 and October 31, 2022 (index date) and 1+ follow-up visits with a Long COVID-associated symptom 90 to 365 days after index (follow-up period). Using modified Poisson regression, we examined the probability of Long COVID diagnosis by age, sex, race/ethnicity, language preference, insurance, COVID-19 vaccination status, and hospitalization at index. Within our analytic sample (n = 34,585), 1.9% of patients were diagnosed with Long COVID. Patients who were ≥ 30 years (versus 18-29), hospitalized at index (versus not), or had 8+ healthcare encounters during follow up (versus one) had a higher probability of Long COVID diagnosis. Conversely, patients with non-English language preference (versus English) had a lower probability of diagnosis (aPR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.24, 0.81), as did patients with Medicare (aPR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.39, 0.67) or Medicaid (aPR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.56, 0.89) versus private insurance. Results suggest Long COVID underdiagnosis for patients who experience barriers to care, including patients with a language barrier or public insurance.

studies.title: MiR-223 and miR-323 as biomarkers of inflammatory and neuropsychiatric alterations in long COVID with chronic viral hepatitis.
studies.authors: da Silva, Lucas Lima, Maul, Juliana Cardoso, Paulo, Iolanda Raquel Ferreira, Lewis-Ximenez, Lia Laura et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID involves persistent physical, mental, and functional symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Its biological mechanisms remain poorly understood, particularly with chronic viral hepatitis. This study investigated associations between microRNA (miRNA) expression and mental and physical health outcomes in individuals with Long COVID, considering chronic hepatitis B or C. This cross-sectional study included 80 individuals divided into four groups (n = 20 each): Long COVID, chronic viral hepatitis, Long COVID with hepatitis, and controls. Depression, anxiety, quality of life, fatigue, and functional status were assessed using validated scales, including the Post-COVID Functional Status Scale. Expression of miR-122, miR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 was quantified by RT-qPCR. Associations were evaluated using non-parametric tests and correlation analyses. MiR-143, miR-223, and miR-323 were significantly upregulated in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiRNA expression was associated with mental and physical health outcomes, particularly through a positive correlation between miR-323 expression and anxiety levels in individuals with Long COVID and hepatitis. MiR-223 was the only miRNA significantly overexpressed in this group compared with all other groups, suggesting its potential as a biomarker of coexisting conditions. Depression and anxiety affected up to 75% and 50% of individuals in the Long COVID groups, respectively (p < 0.05).These findings suggest that circulating miRNAs, particularly miR-223, miR-143, and miR-323, are associated with Long COVID in the presence of chronic viral hepatitis and may serve as biomarkers of disease burden and clinical heterogeneity.

studies.title: Targeting lipid metabolism to overcome immunosuppression and enhance immunotherapy or chemotherapy sensitivity in pancreatic cancer: from immunosuppressive mechanisms to therapeutic opportunities.
studies.authors: Zhan, Ting, Liu, Yuanbin, Yan, Juan, Huang, Xiaodong
studies.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), in which immunosuppression and immune evasion lead to poor response to therapies. Lipid metabolism reprogramming is a central feature of PDAC progression and, depending on the lipid species and context, can promote immunosuppression and immune evasion. Here, we summarize the regulation of lipid metabolism in PDAC and the TME and highlight therapeutic targeting potential. KRAS mutations drive the abnormal activation of key molecules such as SREBP1, FASN, and CD36, promoting de novo fatty acid synthesis, cholesterol metabolism, and the uptake of extracellular lipids. Tumor cells evade immune surveillance by upregulating immune checkpoint molecules and suppressing antigen presentation, thereby impairing both innate and adaptive antitumor immunity. Lipid overload triggers lipid competition and lipotoxicity, induces CD8⁺ T-cell exhaustion and promotes the recruitment of immunosuppressive cells such as M2 macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. Pancreatic stellate cells and peritumoral adipocytes undergo profound lipid metabolic reprogramming and influence the lipid metabolism of PDAC cells and immune function through mechanisms such as paracrine signaling, thereby further reinforcing the immunosuppressive microenvironment. Lipid metabolism interventions such as targeting fatty acid synthesis, cholesterol metabolism, and lipid peroxidation-driven ferroptosis in combination with chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy have shown promise in preclinical models. Targeting lipid metabolism can reshape the immunosuppressive microenvironment and enhance the sensitivity to PD-1 blockade and gemcitabine, significantly improving antitumor efficacy. In the future, combining spatial metabolomics and single cell lipidomics may reveal the interactions between lipid metabolism and the immune system and explore the mechanisms underlying the lipid metabolic interaction networks among tumor-immune-and stromal cells.

studies.title: A novel interprofessional experience caring for post-intensive care and long COVID patients: the optimal clinic experience.
studies.authors: Bouajram, Rima, McGowan, Samuel, Witt, Leah J, Block, Brian et al.
studies.abstract: This short report describes the development of an interprofessional ambulatory care clinic with an interprofessional education program at an academic medical center providing comprehensive care to patients previously hospitalized in the intensive care unit (ICU) or with COVID-19 from May 2020 to May 2026. The OPTIMAL Clinic (lOng COVID/PosT-Icu MultidisciplinAry cLinic) was created during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, with limited staff and temporary funding. Our team consisted of clinical pharmacy and physician trainees, nurse practitioners, occupational therapists, physical therapists, pharmacists, physicians, and social workers, who collaborated strategically and synergistically to optimize patient care. Across repeated evaluations, the clinic model was associated with increased preventive care and financial sustainability, and decreased emergency department visits and unplanned hospitalizations. Our interprofessional education program achieved high ratings from trainees in preceptor support, onboarding, clinical activities, and interprofessional education. Our OPTIMAL clinic exemplifies a model for interprofessional care and education for the support of complex patients after ICU or COVID-19 hospitalizations.

studies.title: The role of the JAK/STAT pathway in the pathogenesis and treatment of post-COVID autoimmune syndromes.
studies.authors: Bruno, Lorenza, Di Berardino, Marta, Cafaro, Giacomo, Pozzolo, Roberto Dal et al.
studies.abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has not only resulted in acute respiratory illness but has also led to a growing population of individuals affected by persistent, debilitating symptoms, collectively known as post-COVID syndrome or "Long COVID". This condition presents with a variety of manifestations, including fatigue, joint pain, cognitive disturbances, and dysautonomia, often mimicking autoimmune and neuroinflammatory disorders. Recent research highlights the Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) signalling pathway as a central mediator in the inflammatory cascade triggered by SARS-CoV-2 infection. This review explores the dual role of the JAK/STAT pathway in both the acute phase of COVID-19 and its potential contribution to post-infectious autoimmune phenomena. We summarize the current understanding of JAK inhibitors (JAKi) as therapeutic agents for mitigating hyperinflammation during active infection and examine their emerging role in the management of post-COVID syndromes, particularly in cases with pulmonary involvement and features overlapping with fibromyalgia and chronic fatigue syndrome. Moreover, we discuss the safety profile of JAKi, their impact on vaccine immunogenicity, and the implications of autoantibody formation targeting the autonomic nervous system. Understanding the immunopathological mechanisms underpinning post-COVID may not only inform therapeutic strategies but also illuminate broader pathways involved in chronic autoimmune conditions.

studies.title: Detection of SARS-CoV-2 in Semen Months After COVID-19: Potential Evidence of Low-Level Replicative Persistence.
studies.authors: Furtado, Marcelo H, Souza, Fernanda R, Andrade, Lidia M, Mendes, Bárbara P et al.
studies.abstract: Viral persistence is considered one of the key mechanisms driving long COVID symptoms. The male genital tract (MGT), particularly the testis, is an immune-privileged site that may serve as a viral reservoir for SARS-CoV-2. However, the presence of SARS-CoV-2 in semen and its long-term infectiousness remains controversial. We aimed to investigate the long-term presence and potential replicative activity of SARS-CoV-2 in semen, evaluating whether the virus can persist and maintain low-level culture signals in the MGT well beyond the acute phase of infection. This observational, prospective, cross-sectional study included 38 men treated at Mater Dei Hospital, Brazil, between October 2020 and October 2021, who had recovered from mild to moderate COVID-19 and consented to participate. Semen samples were collected from mildly symptomatic participants at approximately 1 month (15- 45 days), 3 months, and 6 months after symptom onset. The moderately symptomatic group provided a single sample approximately 6 months post-infection. Semen analysis and SARS-CoV-2 detection were performed using RT-qPCR, followed by viral isolation in Vero CCL-81 cells. Potential viral persistence and replication signals were evaluated through immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). SARS-CoV-2 was detected by RT-qPCR in 21 of 38 patients (55%), with high cycle threshold (Ct 38-39) values observed for more than 6 months post-infection. Following inoculation into Vero cell cultures, a low-level in vitro expansion of viral copies was identified in a subset of samples from mild and moderate patients. The potential presence of the virus was further supported by the presence of viral proteins via immunofluorescence and the identification of structures morphologically compatible with coronavirus-like particles by TEM. This study provides evidence of the long-term persistence of viral RNA and culture-derived signals suggestive of restricted or low-level replicative activity in semen. These findings suggest that the MGT may serve as a viral reservoir, highlighting the importance of longitudinal semen analysis for monitoring viral persistence and reservoir dynamics after clinical recovery.

studies.title: Understanding the Support Needs of People With Long COVID: A Qualitative Study in Aotearoa New Zealand.
studies.journal: Health expectations : an international journal of public participation in health care and health policy
studies.authors: McKenzie, Fiona, Yee, Bailey, Ellison-Lupena, Rochelle, Firestone, Ridvan et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a multi-system condition that affects an increasing number of individuals. Little is known about the support needs of people living with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences and healthcare access challenges of people with long COVID to better inform service design. Co-design methodology was used, informed by the Stanford Design Thinking process and knowledge mobilisation approaches. Participants were recruited via snowballing, through professional networks and support groups. People with lived experience of long COVID were invited to participate in a 2-h workshop, facilitated by researchers, conducted between March and September 2024. Participants were asked to create a depiction of their experience of long COVID and describe their creation to the group; descriptions were audio-recorded, transcribed and thematically analysed. The inclusion of people with lived experience of long COVID as co-investigators ensured that the study was designed and conducted to forefront their knowledge and experience. Eight workshops were conducted, including 30 participants, between March and August 2024. Of these, 25 (83%) were female; of the 25 who provided their age, most were aged 45 to 64 years (n = 18, 72%), four (16%) were aged 25 to 44 years and three (12%) aged 65 years or older. Five key themes emerged: (i) lack of assistance; (ii) systemic barriers; (iii) absence of long COVID clinics; (iv) financial strain; and (v) low quality of care. A sixth theme identified personal coping strategies. Individuals with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand face major barriers to care, including inadequate services, financial hardship, and fragmented healthcare pathways. Findings support improved pathways and primary health care education in long COVID. A person-centred, coordinated, and accessible model of care is needed. The study was designed with two people with lived experience of long COVID included as co-investigators, and a further one on the Advisory Board. All participants had lived experience of long COVID.

studies.title: The impact of SARS-CoV-2 on fatigue and quality of life in the pre-vaccination era: prevalence of post COVID-19 condition up to one year after infection in a Dutch population-based serosurveillance cohort.
studies.authors: van Hagen, Cheyenne C E, Mutubuki, Elizabeth N, de Bruijn, Siméon, Vos, Eric R A et al.
studies.abstract: While previous population-based studies have assessed post-acute sequelae after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), none have investigated health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and (extreme) fatigue after severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection during the pre-vaccination era. Using a nationwide seroepidemiological study, we investigated endpoints linked to post-COVID-19 condition in the general Dutch population up to one year after infection, including symptomatic and asymptomatic infections among unvaccinated individuals early in the pandemic. Participants that were not (yet) vaccinated and aged ≥ 15 years were selected from the February 2021 round of the PIENTER Corona cohort study. We assessed associations between time since serologically-identified SARS-CoV-2 infection and health utility, mental health, physical health and fatigue. To enable comparison across the full range of each outcome, we defined cut-off points for multivariable logistic regression models at every 5% increment (5-75%) along the cumulative distribution of uninfected individuals. At the lowest 15% cut-off, significant differences between uninfected (n = 4,569) and infected ≤ 4 months ago (n = 351) were observed for health utility (odds ratio [95% confidence interval]: 1.6 [1.2-2.2]), physical health (1.9 [1.5-2.5]) and fatigue (1.6 [1.3-2.1]), but not for mental health. There were no significant differences between uninfected and infected > 4-12 months ago (n = 327) for all outcomes, with post-hoc analysis showing power to detect differences down to 7%. In this population-based cohort during the first pandemic year, unvaccinated individuals infected with SARS-CoV-2 ≤ 4 months ago reported poorer health utility and physical health, and more severe fatigue compared to those uninfected. For those infected > 4 and up to 12 months ago statistically significant differences could not be detected in our analysis, suggesting a relatively low post-COVID-19 condition population prevalence up to one year after infection. studies.title: Towards normalization of cognitive function and psychiatric morbidity in patients with neurological symptoms post COVID-19: a longitudinal study.
studies.journal: European archives of psychiatry and clinical neuroscience
studies.authors: Pignatiello, Siv Elin, Boldingh, Marion, Hornslien, Astrid Gjerdrum, Okkenhaug, Ingvil et al.
studies.abstract: Few studies of cognitive impairment in COVID-19 convalescents have assessed patients longitudinally. The aim of this study was to examine the course of performance-based cognitive functions from 6 (T1) to 12 (T2) months after COVID-19 in patients compared with healthy controls, and to investigate the effect of psychiatric diagnosis and fatigue on cognitive function trajectories. Eighty-one patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection reporting neurological symptoms were assessed at T1 and 67 patients at T2 with neuropsychological assessment and a semi-structured psychiatric interview. Fatigue was assessed using the Giessener Beschwerdebogen questionnaire (GBB). Sixty-one, confirmed SARS-CoV-2 antibody negative, healthy controls underwent neuropsychological assessment and completed GBB. At T1, patients performed significantly (p < 0.001 to 0.031) worse across the different cognitive domains, except for verbal fluency, than healthy controls. At T2, there were no significant differences between the two groups in either cognitive domain. Patients improved significantly from T1 to T2 on 7 of 8 domain scores (p < 0.001 to 0.033) and fatigue scores (p = 0.003). The frequency of psychiatric disorders decreased from 40% to 21%. Having a psychiatric diagnosis at T2 and/or delirium during acute COVID-19 significantly predicted a less favourable cognitive function course. These results suggest cognitive function, psychiatric morbidity and fatigue improve one year after COVID-19. Patients with ongoing psychiatric disorder and/or sequela following COVID-19-related delirium may constitute a vulnerable subgroup for non-improvement of cognitive function and should be specifically targeted for rehabilitation and treatment. The study was registered the 09th of October 2020 at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT04576351).

studies.title: Long COVID: A Modified Delphi Consensus on Definition, Burden, Diagnosis and Management in Southeast Asia.
studies.authors: Burhan, Erlina, Chew, Huck Chin, Isbaniah, Fathiyah, Jogulu, Sathya Rao et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a heterogeneous post-infectious condition following acute severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. Ongoing uncertainty around its definition, burden, diagnosis and management complicates clinical recognition and care in Southeast Asia. A modified Delphi consensus study was conducted with twelve experts from six Southeast Asian countries to develop regional guidance on long COVID. Consensus was predefined as ≥ 80% agreement, corresponding to at least 10 of 12 experts selecting the same response in multiple-choice questions or indicating agreement on Likert-scale questions (e.g. agree/strongly agree, most important/more important, relevant/highly relevant). Questions that reached consensus were removed from the subsequent round, while unresolved questions were revised, consolidated, or expanded. In the final round, a post hoc descriptive category, 'moderate endorsement', was applied to Likert-scale questions that had not reached consensus, with 'important' as the midpoint category of the five-point importance scale ('most important' to 'least important'), to capture responses judged important but falling short of the consensus threshold. Consensus was reached for all 'definition', 'burden' and 'management' theme questions and most 'diagnosis' questions. Experts defined long COVID as unexplained symptoms persisting for > 3 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection, distinct from post-acute COVID-19, with no minimum severity threshold requirement. Long COVID was recognised as affecting approximately 6%-10% of individuals after SARS-CoV-2 infection, consistent with published WHO and KSID estimates; clinical evaluation and symptom-guided testing were recommended for its diagnosis. Hospitalisation during acute COVID-19 was identified as a risk factor for developing long COVID. The experts recommended multidisciplinary, symptom-directed care, rehabilitation, pacing and follow-up. Vaccination and reinfection prevention were supported as important long COVID risk-reduction strategies, and early antiviral treatment should be considered to prevent severe acute illness and hospitalisation in high-risk individuals. Consensus was not reached on the past medical history required for diagnosis; moderate endorsement was observed for booster status, absence of early antiviral treatment, pre-COVID health assessment and standardised patient-reported outcome tools. This Delphi study provides a practical regional consensus framework for long COVID in Southeast Asia.

studies.title: Development and initial content validation of the Vienna post-exertional malaise questionnaire: an iterative mixed-methods study.
studies.journal: Quality of life research : an international journal of quality of life aspects of treatment, care and rehabilitation
studies.authors: Pimminger, Theresa, Ahrens-Schwabe, Annika, Fragner, Tobias, Brandl, Tobias et al.
studies.abstract: Post-exertional malaise (PEM) is a multidimensional exertion-response pattern involving diverse triggers, variable onset, and prolonged recovery. This study developed and content-validated the Vienna Post-Exertional Malaise (VPEM) Questionnaire, a patient-reported outcome measure assessing functional decline, recovery, crash-associated symptoms, and pacing adaptations in ME/CFS. An iterative mixed-methods instrument-development study combined quantitative ratings and qualitative feedback across sequential evaluation cycles. An initial 13-item draft, informed by existing PEM, fatigue, and functional-capacity instruments and consensus literature, was evaluated by individuals with ME/CFS or Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) using Likert ratings, open-ended feedback, and interviews. Quantitative data were summarised descriptively, and qualitative data were analysed using deductive-inductive structuring content analysis. Revisions were documented in revision matrices. The revised instrument was evaluated by an interdisciplinary expert panel using domain-level and item-level ratings of relevance and clarity. Twelve individuals with ME/CFS and one individual with PCS fulfilling ME/CFS criteria evaluated the questionnaire. Ratings showed high approval for length (92.3%) and terminology (76.9%), while completeness and clarity were more heterogeneous. Qualitative findings identified ambiguities in distinguishing PEM from non-specific fatigue, missing trigger domains, and insufficient representation of intra-individual variability. After revision, the expert panel (n = 11) rated PEM coverage as complete or largely complete (100%) and the multidimensional structure as suitable or very suitable (90.9%). Item-level ratings showed high relevance (S-CVI/Ave = 0.96), whereas clarity ratings were more variable (S-CVI/Ave = 0.82). The VPEM Questionnaire operationalises PEM as multidimensional post-exertional deterioration. Findings support initial content and face validity, warranting further psychometric validation.

studies.title: A New Outlook on Infection-Associated Chronic Conditions and Illnesses.
studies.authors: Bertolli, Jeanne, Hinckley, Alison F, Mead, Paul S, Patel, Pragna et al.
studies.abstract: Infection-associated chronic conditions and illnesses (IACCI) encompass several debilitating syndromes with overlapping symptoms that have been identified and documented for decades, primarily following infectious disease outbreaks. Conditions following infection that are diagnosed with objective clinical tests have been relatively well characterized and accepted by the medical establishment, although the relationship to infection can be challenging to establish. In contrast, syndromes that lack objective tests, even when following a recognized infection, such as myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome, post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome, and dysautonomia, are underrecognized and often stigmatized. The COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent recognition of Long COVID as the newest example of IACCI offer new opportunities to address all aspects of IACCI. Lessons learned from the government's multi-agency public health response to Long COVID could be beneficial to ensure readiness for the long-term consequences of sporadic infections, outbreaks, and future pandemics.

studies.title: Implementation effectiveness of the Long COVID and Fatiguing Illnesses Recovery Program (LC&FIRP): a multimodal Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes (ECHO) model for clinician learning.
studies.authors: Zuber, Alexandra, Rothwell, Jonathan T, Godino, Job G, Samaniego, Jane C et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID and other infection-associated chronic conditions (IACC) present management challenges for primary care clinicians and often require patient access to multidisciplinary specialists. To strengthen primary care capacity, the Long COVID and Fatiguing Illnesses Recovery Program (LC&FIRP) implemented a multi-modal learning model combining Extension for Community Healthcare Outcomes (ECHO) case-based learning with complementary educational modalities. The ECHO learning component was evaluated for effectiveness in a Type II hybrid design randomized control trial, and an implementation evaluation assessed implementation of the full LC&FIRP model to inform future implementation and scale-up. We conducted a qualitatively driven mixed-methods implementation evaluation of the LC&FIRP model, assessing acceptability, feasibility, fidelity, sustainability, and scalability. Participants comprised clinicians from a federally qualified health center serving predominantly uninsured, low-income, and medically underserved patients in San Diego, CA. All trial clinicians were offered monthly webinars and quarterly asynchronous online short courses; intervention clinicians were additionally offered weekly ECHO sessions. Data sources were session surveys at the end of every session or short-course, quarterly clinician follow-up surveys, and interviews with participants, subject matter experts (SMEs) and clinic administrators at program end. Acceptability findings reflected high clinician satisfaction and perceived utility of the weekly and monthly offerings but moderate sustained engagement and negligible participation in the quarterly short courses. Clinicians valued most the interactive peer exchange; practical diagnostic and treatment approaches; and lessons from SMEs with lived experience. Feasibility barriers included competing clinical and administrative demands and the time commitment required for participation. Most program components were implemented with fidelity but fewer weekly ECHO sessions and case presentations were delivered than planned. Sustainability and scalability showed early promise with the continuation of weekly and monthly offerings after trial end, but future barriers remain. This study demonstrates that a multi-modal program combining ECHO case-based learning with complementary educational offerings may be feasibly implemented and is acceptable to clinicians for supporting primary care management of complex chronic conditions, although sustaining engagement and scaling the model will require adaptations to reduce participation burden and resource requirements.

studies.title: Treatment strategies in pancreatic adenosquamous carcinoma: a systematic review and pooled analysis of individual cases.
studies.authors: Gao, Xiang Yu, Ganatra, Nency, Abdelhakeem, Ahmed, Tran, Nugyen et al.
studies.abstract: Pancreatic adenosquamous carcinoma (PASC) is a rare 1-4% of all pancreatic cancers and an aggressive pancreatic malignancy characterized by mixed adenocarcinoma and squamous histologies. Even after surgical intervention, patients with PASC have a lower median overall survival (mOS) than those with the more prevalent pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Secondary to its rarity, there are no formal guidelines, published clinical trials, or systematic reviews on treatment strategies for managing PASC. The primary objective was to assess mOS in months among patients with local non-metastatic disease treated with different modalities. Secondary objectives were to assess differences in mOS between chemotherapy regimens and according to surgical resectability and initial tumor size, as well as to evaluate the independent association between chemotherapy and overall survival using multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression. A comprehensive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Google Scholar, and Cochrane Library for all full-text articles up to July 2026 identified 503 studies that were conducted globally. 72 case series and reports that met inclusion criteria were selected following PRISMA guidelines. A total of 89 patients from 72 publications were included. The median age was 66 (interquartile range, 60-72) years, 49 patients were male, and the median tumor diameter was 48 (interquartile range, 35-74) mm. Forty-nine patients received chemotherapy and 55 underwent surgical resection. Eighty-eight patients had both survival time and vital status and were included in survival analyses, with 56 deaths observed. In the primary treatment-modality analysis, among surgically unresectable patients, mOS was 3.0 months with neither chemotherapy nor radiotherapy, 6.0 months with chemotherapy alone, 13.7 months with radiotherapy alone, and 15.5 months with combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy (P=0.01). Among surgically resectable patients, mOS was 10.8 months with neither chemotherapy nor radiotherapy, 6.7 months with chemotherapy alone, 4.0 months with radiotherapy alone, and 26.0 months with combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy (P=0.03). In the secondary multivariable Cox model, chemotherapy was independently associated with improved overall survival [hazard ratio (HR), 0.41; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.24-0.70; P=0.001], while surgical resection was not independently associated with survival (HR, 1.17; 95% CI: 0.58-2.34; P=0.66). mOS across all patients was 8.0 months (95% CI: 6.5-12.0). Median survival differed significantly according to disease extent, ranging from 33.0 months among patients with borderline resectable disease to 4.0 months among patients with metastatic disease (P=0.0004). Restricted mean survival at 24 months was 15.6 months with chemotherapy versus 8.2 months without chemotherapy. The association between chemotherapy and improved survival remained significant across most sensitivity analyses. Among patients with unresectable disease, mOS was 18.0 months with S-1, 5.4 months with gemcitabine, and 4.0 months with 5-fluorouracil (P=0.09). Combined chemotherapy and radiotherapy were associated with the longest mOS among both surgically resectable and unresectable patients in the primary treatment-modality analysis.

studies.title: Persistently activated virus-specific CD8 T cells indicate antigen-driven immune aberrations in long COVID.
studies.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
studies.authors: Painter, Mark M, Reeg, David B, Douek, Naomi R, Gray-Gaillard, Sophie L et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) affects millions of people worldwide, yet its driving mechanisms remain incompletely defined and no treatment has been approved. Persistence of SARS-CoV-2 and reactivation of herpesviruses have been implicated in LC, but direct detection of these viral antigens in blood and tissues has been challenging. T cells are exquisitely sensitive to viral antigens, survey organs throughout the body, and can be readily sampled in peripheral blood. Using high-dimensional spectral flow cytometry and single-cell sequencing approaches with multiplexed peptide/HLA tetramers, we profiled virus-specific T cells from hundreds of people with LC and recovered controls. We identified a subset of people with LC that maintained elevated activation of CD8 T cells targeting SARS-CoV-2 spike and/or lytic antigens from Epstein-Barr virus, but not other viral specificities. Spike-specific cells in LC expressed genes linked to TCR stimulation, terminal effector differentiation, and exhaustion and demonstrated reduced functionality upon cognate peptide stimulation

studies.title: Sex-Specific Plasma Proteomic Alterations Underpin Distinct COVID-19 Progression and Post-COVID-19 Condition.
studies.authors: Lu, Qiuhan, Zhang, Yi, Yi, Shiyu, Wu, Yuwen et al.
studies.abstract: Sex differences in COVID-19 and its sequelae remain poorly understood, which hinders targeted therapies. We performed plasma proteomic analyses of 69 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 and 30 healthy controls from a prospective Chinese cohort. The UK Biobank and Mount Sinai Biobank were employed for validation and provided insights into the progression mechanisms. Biological and tissue enrichment analyses characterized sex-specific pathways and tissue-enriched proteins. We identified ANXA11, a molecular tether that physically links RNA granules to lysosomal membranes to enable their long-distance transport and local translation, as a protein associated with male-specific susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Decreased ANXA11 protein levels were linked to higher risk of infection in males, replicated in the UK Biobank. Sex-specific proteomic alterations revealed distinct biological responses, including glycosylation-related pathways in females and cell adhesion, platelet-leukocyte interactions, and inflammatory responses in males. Sex-specific protein changes were also associated with distinct post-COVID-19 symptom profiles. ANXA11 was identified as a novel protein associated with the male-specific susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection. Sex-specific protein changes revealed distinct mechanistic differences between male and female patients in COVID-19 progression and may explain sex differences in post-COVID-19 conditions.

studies.title: Incidence and risk factors of acute respiratory illness associated with influenza, COVID-19, and respiratory syncytial virus within a birth cohort study.
studies.authors: Bird, Bryden, Thorn, Louise, Aminisani, Nayyereh, Wood, Tim et al.
studies.abstract: Influenza virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are leading causes of acute respiratory infections (ARIs). New Zealand's coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) public health measures disrupted the circulation of these viruses in 2020-2021, creating a rare opportunity to explore the impact of potential immunity gaps on age-specific infection risk. We analyzed data from 843 participants aged between 0 and 4 years enrolled in the Southern Hemisphere Influenza and Vaccine Effectiveness Research and Surveillance 3 (SHIVERS-III) birth cohort, a longitudinal community-based study in New Zealand, during 2020-2024. During the respiratory season, weekly surveillance captured ARI symptoms and severity. Nasal swabs were collected from symptomatic participants and tested for viral RNA by RT-PCR. Incidence rates (IRs) and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated for the surveillance period and adjusted for age, sex, ethnic group, socioeconomic status, and influenza vaccination status. No influenza or SARS-CoV-2 infections were detected in 2020 and 2021. From 2021 to 2024, RSV had the highest IR during the surveillance period (63.2/100 person-years [PY]; 95% CI, 56.6-69.8), followed by SARS-CoV-2 (39.3/100 PY; 95% CI, 34.5-44) and influenza (35.7/100 PY; 95% CI, 29-42.3). Age influenced infection risk: infants <6 months had the lowest incidence of influenza and RSV, potentially reflecting maternally derived immunity and limited exposure. Risk increased after 6 months of age, peaking at age 1 year for RSV and at age 2 years for influenza. Influenza vaccination lowered symptomatic influenza risk (IRR 0.66; 95% CI, 0.44-1.00). In the New Zealand community setting in the post-COVID-19 era, individual respiratory virus illness patterns differ in children aged 0-4. Influenza vaccine shows protection, and age influences virus-specific risk. Influenza virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are major causes of acute respiratory illness in early childhood, yet current understanding is largely reliant on hospital-based surveillance that underestimates the broader community burden. This study addresses this limitation by providing comprehensive, community-based estimates of incidence, severity, and symptom profiles across these viruses within a single longitudinal birth cohort. By leveraging the unique epidemiological context created by pandemic-related disruptions, it offers important insights into how changes in exposure influence subsequent infection risk and virus circulation. The direct comparison of three major respiratory viruses within the same population highlights distinct age-related risk patterns and disease characteristics. In addition, our research provides real-world evidence of the reduced risk of influenza-associated acute respiratory illness among vaccinated children. These findings strengthen the evidence base for age-targeted immunization strategies and improve understanding of early-life respiratory virus epidemiology.

studies.title: A novel model demonstrating that human immune cells promote multiorgan SARS-CoV-2 dissemination and human T cells limit anti-viral innate immunity.
studies.authors: Wolabaugh, Amber, Agashe, Vrushali V, Wang, Zicheng, Danzl, Nichole M et al.
studies.abstract: Despite extensive studies, many questions remain regarding the pathology and mechanisms behind Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), and particularly on post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC). Because existing mouse models cannot recapitulate human immune responses, we developed a human immune system (HIS) mouse model with physiologic expression of hACE2.

studies.title: "I Picked Myself Up Through Prayer and Soups": Factors Impeding and Enhancing Long COVID Recovery Among Latinos in South Texas.
studies.authors: Alvarez-Hernandez, Luis R, Clark, Loren C, Uzoh, Hemma, Gonzales, Xavier F et al.
studies.abstract: We aimed to understand what factors have impeded and enhanced Long COVID recovery among Latinos in South Texas. Through community partners, 78 participants were part of seven focus groups. We analyzed the data following Braun and Clarke's Reflexive Thematic Analysis. Factors that impeded recovery were: (1) Working while ill due to labor needs, expectations, and limited safety nets, (2) Mistrusting health care due to invalidating systemic barriers, (3) Grieving former self, and (4) Obsessing over the known and unknown. Factors that enhanced recovery were: (1) Focusing on a conscious fight to preserve life, (2) Leveraging cultural knowledge to reconnect with their sense of wholeness as a person, (3) Choosing Western medicine as one method of healing, and (4) Relying on God and trusted ones. Long COVID recovery interventions among South Texas Latinos must account for structural and social determinants of health and cultural ways of healing.

studies.title: Converging pathomechanisms link SARS-CoV-2 infection with major neurodegenerative diseases.
studies.authors: HeFeng, Feng Q, Martí-Sarrias, Andrea, Guvenilir, Heval Atas, de Sá, Renata Baptista Vieira et al.
studies.abstract: Neurological complications are among typical clinical manifestations, both during the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-term post-acute COVID-19 sequelae, i.e., Long COVID. A growing body of evidence connects SARS-CoV-2 infection to systemic inflammation, peripheral immune dysregulation, functional alteration of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), neuroinflammatory processes, mitochondrial dysfunction and pathological protein aggregation, all of which are central to the pathogenesis of major neurodegenerative diseases. In this review, we discuss the converging shared underlying molecular mechanisms that link the 'acute' SARS-CoV-2 infection that often only lasts for days and 'chronic' neurodegenerative diseases that often take decades to develop. We further review human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs)-derived brain organoid and BBB models for Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) as well as artificial intelligence (AI)-facilitated knowledge graph methods that are used to hypothesize and validate the potential mechanistic links. We propose that besides the established links between viral infections and neurodegenerative or neuroinflammatory conditions, such as Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in multiple sclerosis or herpes zoster in AD, SARS-CoV-2 infection might be another important factor driving the future burden of the most common neurodegenerative diseases.

studies.title: Metformin and Severe Post-COVID-19 Outcomes Among Individuals With Diabetes Mellitus.
studies.authors: Dozier, Zachary B, Wang, Lin-Chiun, Ji, Yunwen, Anzalone, A Jerrod et al.
studies.abstract: We evaluated the relationship between metformin, one of the most commonly prescribed medications for individuals with diabetes, and COVID-19 sequelae. We evaluated a retrospective cohort of individuals in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative with Type 2 diabetes mellitus and COVID-19 who were prescribed metformin or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP4i) at least 30 days before the onset of acute COVID-19 between 1 October 2021, and 15 November 2023. We compared the 12-month cumulative incidence of Long COVID diagnosis (ICD-10 U09.9: Post COVID-19 condition, unspecified), probable Long COVID (based on a model-derived phenotype), and mortality between individuals prescribed metformin versus DPP4i. We applied Super Learner and targeted maximum likelihood estimation to obtain risk ratios while adjusting for covariates of interest. In our sample of 53 332 individuals with Type 2 diabetes and COVID-19, we found that metformin prescription was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality after COVID-19 (adjusted risk ratio [aRR]: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.51, 0.73). We also observed that metformin users, compared to DPP4i users, had a slightly lower risk of probable Long COVID (aRR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.81, 0.94) but did not detect a significant relationship with the clinically defined outcome of Long COVID diagnosis (aRR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.68, 1.20). These findings support the hypothesis that metformin prescription during acute COVID-19 may be associated with lower mortality among adults with diabetes.

studies.title: [Insights on biological markers in post-COVID condition: a scope review].
studies.authors: Amorim, Amanda Dos Santos de, Porto, Evailson Ferreira, Oliveira, Márcio Vasconcelos
studies.abstract: Post-COVID condition (PCC) is characterized by the persistence of symptoms following acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. This scoping review aimed to identify and compile scientific evidence on biomarkers associated with PCC to elucidate its pathophysiology and support clinical diagnosis and management. A systematic search was conducted in six databases (PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, BVS, Embase, and ScienceDirect), selecting original studies published between May 2020 and April 2024. Observational studies investigating clinical and prognostic biomarkers in PCC patients were included. After applying eligibility criteria, 10 studies were selected. The most frequently reported biomarkers were interleukins IL-1β, IL-6, and IL-8, proteins associated with persistent inflammation and immune dysfunction. Other relevant markers included D-dimer, C-reactive protein (CRP), VEGF-A, and matrix metalloproteinases. Results highlight that inflammatory biomarkers play a key role in characterizing and monitoring PCC. It is concluded that identifying accessible biomarkers, easily integrated into clinical practice, can aid in developing more effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. A condição pós-COVID (CPC) é caracterizada pela persistência de sintomas após a infecção aguda pelo SARS-CoV-2. Esta revisão de escopo teve como objetivo identificar e reunir evidências científicas sobre biomarcadores associados à CPC, visando esclarecer sua fisiopatologia e apoiar o diagnóstico e manejo clínico. A busca sistemática foi realizada em seis bases de dados (PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, BVS, Embase e ScienceDirect), selecionando artigos originais publicados entre maio de 2020 e abril de 2024. Foram incluídos estudos observacionais que investigaram biomarcadores clínicos e prognósticos em pacientes com CPC. Após a aplicação dos critérios de elegibilidade, 10 estudos foram selecionados. Os biomarcadores mais frequentemente relatados foram as interleucinas IL-1β, IL-6 e IL-8, interleucinas associadas à inflamação persistente e disfunção imunológica. Outros marcadores relevantes incluíram D-dímero, proteína C reativa (PCR), VEGF-A e metaloproteinases. Os resultados reforçam que os biomarcadores inflamatórios desempenham papel essencial na caracterização e monitoramento da CPC. Conclui-se que a identificação de biomarcadores acessíveis e integráveis à prática clínica pode auxiliar na elaboração de estratégias diagnósticas e terapêuticas mais eficazes. La condición post-COVID (CPC) se caracteriza por la persistencia de síntomas tras la infección aguda por SARS-CoV-2. Esta revisión de alcance tuvo como objetivo identificar y recopilar evidencia científica sobre biomarcadores asociados con la CPC, con el fin de esclarecer su fisiopatología y apoyar el diagnóstico y manejo clínico. Se realizó una búsqueda sistemática en seis bases de datos (PubMed, Scopus, SciELO, BVS, Embase y ScienceDirect), seleccionando estudios originales publicados entre mayo de 2020 y abril de 2024. Se incluyeron estudios observacionales que investigaron biomarcadores clínicos y pronósticos en pacientes con CPC. Tras aplicar los criterios de elegibilidad, se seleccionaron 10 estudios. Los biomarcadores más frecuentemente reportados fueron las interleucinas IL-1β, IL-6 e IL-8, proteínas asociadas con inflamación persistente y disfunción inmunológica. Otros marcadores relevantes incluyeron D-dímero, proteína C reactiva (PCR), VEGF-A y metaloproteinasas. Los resultados destacan que los biomarcadores inflamatorios desempeñan un papel clave en la caracterización y el monitoreo de la CPC. Se concluye que la identificación de biomarcadores accesibles e integrables en la práctica clínica puede contribuir al desarrollo de estrategias diagnósticas y terapéuticas más eficaces.

studies.title: Risk factors for Post-COVID-19 Syndrome in patients hospitalized for severe acute respiratory syndrome: systematic review and meta-analysis.
studies.authors: Soares, Sofia Ramos, Souza, Rafaela Santos Nogueira de, Barros, Loreena Uchôa Lira, Camboim, Felipe Miranda et al.
studies.abstract: This study aims to identify the risk factors associated with the development of post-COVID-19 syndrome in patients discharged from hospitalizations due to severe acute respiratory syndrome. A systematic review of observational studies published between 2020 and 2023 was carried out in six databases. The relative risk values of each factor investigated were evaluated in the meta-analysis using the random-effects model; 1,010 publications were identified, with 45 studies included in the qualitative analysis and seven studies in the meta-analysis. These studies evaluated the association between post-COVID-19 syndrome and factors such as the severity and number of symptoms of the disease in the acute phase, sex, and previous comorbidities. The results showed that female gender (RR 1.52; 95%CI 1.26-1.85), the presence of hypertension (RR 1.25; 95%CI 1.06-1.49) and a longer hospital stay (RR 1.01; 95%CI 1.01-1.03) were associated with the development of the syndrome. Female patients discharged from hospital due to COVID-19, with longer hospital stays and hypertension should be monitored to identify the development of post-COVID-19 syndrome, enabling timely interventions. Este estudo tem como objetivo identificar os fatores de risco associados ao desenvolvimento da síndrome pós-COVID-19 em egressos de internações por Síndrome Respiratória Aguda Grave. Foi realizada revisão sistemática de estudos observacionais publicados entre 2020 e 2023 em seis bases de dados. Os valores dos riscos relativos de cada fator investigado foram avaliados na metanálise através do modelo de efeitos aleatórios; 1.010 publicações foram identificadas, sendo 45 estudos incluídos na análise qualitativa e sete estudos na metanálise. Estes estudos avaliaram a associação entre a síndrome pós-COVID-19 e fatores como a gravidade e o número de sintomas da doença na fase aguda, o sexo e comorbidades prévias. Os resultados apontaram que o sexo feminino (RR 1,52; IC95% 1,26-1,85), a presença de hipertensão (RR 1,25; IC95% 1,06-1,49) e um maior tempo de internação (RR 1,01; IC95% 1.01-1,03) estavam associados ao desenvolvimento da síndrome. Egressos de internação por COVID-19 do sexo feminino, com maior tempo de internação e hipertensão deverão ser monitorados para identificar o desenvolvimento da síndrome pós-COVID-19, possibilitando intervenções em tempo oportuno. Este estudio tiene como objetivo identificar los factores de riesgo asociados al desarrollo del síndrome post-COVID-19 en pacientes dados de alta de hospitalizaciones por síndrome respiratorio agudo severo. Se realizó una revisión sistemática de estudios observacionales publicados entre 2020 y 2023 en seis bases de datos. Los valores de riesgo relativo de cada factor investigado se evaluaron en el metaanálisis utilizando un modelo de efectos aleatorios. Se identificaron 1.010 publicaciones, de las cuales 45 estudios se incluyeron en el análisis cualitativo y siete en el metaanálisis. Estos estudios evaluaron la asociación entre el síndrome post-COVID-19 y factores como la gravedad y el número de síntomas de la enfermedad en la fase aguda, el sexo y las comorbilidades preexistentes. Los resultados indicaron que el sexo femenino (RR 1,52; IC95% 1,26-1,85), la presencia de hipertensión (RR 1,25; IC95% 1,06-1,49) y una estancia hospitalaria más prolongada (RR 1,01; IC95% 1,01-1,03) se asociaron con el desarrollo del síndrome. Las pacientes dadas de alta tras una hospitalización por COVID-19, con estancias hospitalarias más prolongadas e hipertensión, deben ser monitorizadas para identificar el desarrollo del síndrome post-COVID-19 y permitir intervenciones oportunas.
